articleTitle: Investigating Principle Component Analysis Impact on the Performance of Machine Learning Classifiers: A Health Informatics Application
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Principal Components Analysis (PCA) is a popular dimensionality reduction and feature selection technique. It works by swiping non-informative features while retaining those that are still potentially useful. However, regardless of its wide applications in statistical analysis, the influence of PCA on the performance of classification algorithms has been rarely studied, particularly in the domain of medical image classification. In this paper, we present a thorough analysis of the influence of applying PCA on the classification of medical images. The dataset used in this study consists of thousands of images that represent four types of blood cells. These images are used to train three machine-learning classifier models after transforming images into numerical vectors using a CNN pre-trained embedding algorithm, where each image is encoded using one thousand numerical vectors. The study involves building three classification models using (1) K-nearest Neighbor (KNN), (2) Logistic Regression (LR), and (3) Random Forests (RF). Each model was built twice, once after the application of PCA to reduce the dimensionality of the embedded features and once with the original embedded features. The performance of each model is evaluated using Classification accuracy, F1, AUC, Recall, precision, and specificity metrics. The recorded performance is then compared to drawing a decisive conclusion.

articleTitle: Unveiling Android Malware: A Deep Learning Perspective Using RNN and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The advent and increasing popularity of Android devices have brought about undesirable mobile malware and its attendant applications that constitutes a danger to society in terms of privacy and information leakage. Because the Android open-source OS is attractive to criminals, it seems impossible for old methods of virus detection to be effective as they used to be. The present study tackles this vital problem by offering an innovative enhancement that uses deep learning algorithms: recurrent neural networks and long short-term memory networks for android malware detection. New solid classification schema was created which focused on the meta-information of applications in order to differentiate entre benign and malicious apps. In our experiments, both RNN and LSTM models yielded improvements in performance metrics which suggests that they can be used to counter the current computer malware challenges. This study adds to the body of knowledge available on the detection of malware and lays the foundation for other studies designed to employ other couplings of deep learning algorithms in further boosting the security of Android applications.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease Using EfficientNet-B3 Architecture with Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: In order to bring forward expansion in both the accuracy and the processing speed of the detection of Alzheimer’s disease, an automated approach for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis with passable EfficientNet-B3 neural network and transfer learning techniques is provided in this work. After direct fitness on a large number of annotated brain images, the model of EfficientNet-B3 is further trained, in an effort to obtain worse depicted quality connected with Alzheimer’s Disease. To hasten the process of training and to make the model fit for this specific task, transfer learning was employed. The results of these experiments prove the efficiency of our approach to the diagnostic Alzheimer’s disease compared to the most advanced and regular deep learning methods. Thus, the model may also withstand the test amidst diverse clinical populations by performing well in dementia classification with precision and recall performance coupled with over 99% accuracy. These findings demonstrate how the EfficientNet-B3 architecture and transfer learning enhance generalization across.

articleTitle: Using Monte Carlo Simulation for Real Estate Price Valuation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Forecasting housing prices holds considerable importance in informing planning decisions at the individual level, within industries, and across the broader economy. Experts use housing prices to assess inflationary patterns or other economic crises. Given the uncertainty in the real estate industry, this study introduces a novel method for predicting home prices using a systematic and quantitative approach. The research employed Monte Carlo Simulation to provide valuable insights for the real estate sector, enabling better decision-making through increased predictive accuracy. This study emphasized using a Monte Carlo simulation as an effective approach for predicting housing values. This study's results showed that Monte Carlo simulations provide greater accuracy than multiple regression analysis in predicting home values. The Monte Carlo Simulation has proven reliable, effectively predicting property values with notable precision, consistency, and dependability.

articleTitle: Decision Support in Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The requirement engineering process starts with an abstract description of the user needs or problems and ends with a detailed and precise specification of these user needs. Therefore, the analyst needs to decide several times during the requirements engineering. The incorrect or inadequate decisions cause software failure or software that partially fulfills the user requirements. Consequently, it is mandatory to integrate the decision-making process at the beginning of software development. In other words, the tradeoffs can be discovered in the software requirements phase, and the alternatives can be identified. Furthermore, the decision-making process requires special attention since it applies to all requirements engineering activities, such as requirements collection, negotiation, prioritization, and planning. This paper emphasizes the advantages of integrating decision-making in Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering (GORE) and mapping the decision-making framework to GORE. Also, the paper discusses whether the decision-making process should be included in one of the GORE phases or an ongoing process covering all GORE phases.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Measuring the Impact of Code Smells on Web Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Code smells are a surface symptom that generally indicates a more serious problem in the software system therefore it is kind of hard to detect them manually so many automated tools are required to get the job done. The study focuses on proposing an empirical study that has been applied on web applications in order to detect the large classes manually based on Michele and Marinescu large classes’ detection strategy as shown in Figure 1. The result of the study was the failure of the first project group due to the inability and agreement to identify large classes, while the second project group succeeded, as the participants agreed to define large classes more precisely, in addition to that the study showed that the process of manually identifying large classes is a very difficult process therefore an automated tools (AI tools) are required to make it easier and more accurate.

articleTitle: Automating the Diagnosis of Cucumber Plant Diseases Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Farmers all over the world struggle to fight plant diseases. However, the incorrect use of pesticides can waste time, effort, and money and can also be very harmful to the environment and human health. In this work, we present an empirical study that involves identifying two pathogens related to Cucumbers plant diseases: Powdery Mildew and Alternaria Cucumerina. The study aims to develop a computer-based solution based on deep learning and machine learning algorithms to detect these diseases. To achieve this, a dataset of hundreds of samples was collected from ordinary farms in Beqaa, an agricultural region 15 KM north of Amman, Jordan. Three machine learning models were created in this study using Support Vector Machines (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), and Multi-layer perceptron algorithms. The constructed models were applied to the dataset after embedding the dataset images using the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) InceptionV3 pre-trained model. The model was tested and evaluated using cross-evaluation and F1-Score, CA, AUC, Precision, Recall, and Specificity, which all showed excellent results, particularly using the SVM algorithm. The constructed methods are intended to be deployed to farms in their field condition environments using a CCTV system that can capture images of plants during growth, which can help identify plant diseases at that right stage, which would save time, effort, and money and reduce the impact of wrong and overuse of pesticides on consumers and the environment.

articleTitle: From Insights to Impact: Business Intelligence’s Influence on Jordan’s Industrial Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study aims to understand how Business Intelligence (BI) systems impact decision-making in Jordan's industrial sector. Despite the growing prevalence of BI systems, their influence on enhancing decision-making processes in the industrial sector remains underexplored. The study evaluates the current adoption and application of BI systems across Jordan's industrial sector, identifies the critical success factors for successful BI implementation, and examines relationships between key BI system variables information quality, service quality, system quality, training quality and decision-making effectiveness decision accuracy, timeliness, strategic alignment. The results reveal that information quality and training quality significantly enhance decision-making effectiveness, including accuracy and strategic alignment, while service quality and system quality show moderate impacts. The study concludes by recommending strategies for improving the use of BI systems to strengthen decision-making capabilities within Jordan's industrial sector.

articleTitle: Efficient Road Status Monitoring in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks: An Optimization Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The number of cars on the road in the world is currently increasing. With the widespread usage of vehicles, a slew of issues inevitably arises. The damage of the road can be annoying to the drivers, and congestion in traffic can waste both fuel and time. It's worth noting that one of the primary causes of car damage and aging is the state of the road surface. Driving comfort and vehicle controllability can be harmed by poor road conditions. As a result, the system of monitoring road status is crucial to reducing congestion in traffic, reducing accident rates, and protecting cars from hazardous road conditions. This paper proposes using a framework based on cloud-fog network architecture, The fog computing network architecture is a dispersed network that may process data at the fog layer to minimize cloud computing's computational load. In addition, using small and large threshold values ( ), Main Authority (MA) deals with the major conditions, and the Sub Authority (SA) deals with the minor conditions.

articleTitle: The Values of Digital Citizenship Among Social Media Users in Jordan: A Case Study of Facebook
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the values of digital citizenship among Jordan's social media users. According to data given by Internet World Stats, the target population was roughly 6.5 million active users in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan. A sample of 1,500 Facebook users was chosen for the year 2024. The current study followed a descriptive analytical method. To achieve its goals, a digital citizenship scale for social media users was created, with 54 items divided into six dimensions: digital access, digital commerce, digital etiquette, digital security/self-protection, digital rights and responsibilities, and digital health and safety. The scale's validity and reliability were both established. The study produced the following results:•Overall, Jordanian social media users have modest levels of digital citizenship principles.•Digital etiquette, digital access, and digital health and safety received intermediate ratings, while digital commerce and digital security received low ratings.•The study found no statistically significant differences in digital citizenship values among social media users based on gender.

articleTitle: Continuous Wavelet Transform Spectral Image Based Epileptic Episode Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Numerous individuals globally, regardless of age, have the neurological condition epilepsy. Recurrent seizures compromised motor and sensory abilities, and a hindered normal lifestyle are all signs of epilepsy. By seeing or manually examining electroencephalogram (EEG) data, neurologists can make the diagnosis of epileptic seizures. In this paper, a continuous wavelet transform spectral image-based epileptic episode classification technique is proposed. The EEG signal was first converted into 227x227 RGB images using CWT. Then these images were used to create an image dataset, and classification was performed using the proposed deep ensemble epileptic seizure classifier (DE_ESC). DE_ESC ensembled Dense_net_169, Dense_net_201, and Inception_V3. This proposed method obtained 100% accuracy (Ac), precision (Pr), recall, and F1 Score, respectively.

articleTitle: Deep Learning content-based search in media files
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The rapid growth of digital multimedia content has created a new demand for technologies that not only process but also sort and locate images and videos amidst the vast amounts of content. Traditional text-based search engines often struggle to retrieve specific visual content based on visual features alone, which has spurred the development of computer vision technologies for content-based image and video retrieval. This work presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a user-friendly application, "Search by visual content," that leverages artificial intelligence (AI) and, more particularly, the deep learning model of YOLOv8. Our application allows users to search multimedia sources such as images and videos not by their names, types, and metadata, but by using similar images or videos as input. It also offers the feature of searching multimedia content containing a certain object inputted in the search box. Our easy-to-use application delivers prompt and accurate search results, and it can function across multiple operating systems as it was made using Python language.

articleTitle: Software Code De-Compilation Techniques and Approaches: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: De-compilation is the process of executable files as input where the de-compilation process tries to get away the source code, or the majority of it, if the file's source code is lost or damaged for whatever cause. De-compilation has many uses such as code recovery, security testing, and errors corrections, however, de-compilation is cautious since it depends on certain approaches and techniques. Nowadays de-compilation done by many automated and semi-automated tools, but the accuracy and the efficiency of it depend on the proposed approaches and techniques to stand in front of reengineering challenges. This paper aims to highlight up-to-date prior contributions in the field where 8 published research papers from May 2020 until May 2023 were collected to investigate the state-of-art. As a result, some of the researchers tend to develop their own tools and others tend to use popular automated with different approaches and techniques where the majority of the researchers focused on C, C++, and JAVA programming languages where 50% were de-compilation on C language.

articleTitle: Intelligent Farm Irrigation and Safety System
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: In recent years, there has been growing interest in utilizing technology to improve agricultural practices and optimize crop yield. One area of focus is the development of intelligent farm irrigation systems that integrate automation, sensing, and control mechanisms to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of farming operations. An important aspect of automated agriculture is the management of irrigation, as well as ensuring the safety of the farming environment. Plastic houses have become a cornerstone in modern agriculture, enabling controlled cultivation environments and increased yields. However, managing these environments efficiently requires a harmonious integration of various factors. This paper proposes an intelligent for irrigation, temperature, humidity, flame, gas detection, and fire alarm functions in a plastic house. The system presented here uses Arduino Microcontroller based system that integrates various sensors technology to monitor soil conditions accompanied by audible and visual alerts. Fire safety is ensured through flame and gas sensors, triggering immediate alerts. Python language was used to write the code for the Arduino microcontroller.

articleTitle: Building Trustworthy AI systems for secure digital health services
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Nowadays, artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly utilized in digital health services, which secure systems to safeguard patient data and ensure reliable service delivery. Our methodology incorporates authoritative artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, strong encryption leads to an opportunity for the development of trustworthy systems, and adherence to healthcare standards like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).Particularly, we utilized convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image analysis and natural language processing (NLP) to understand patient data, to determine the requirement for security, the nature of the data processed by NLP, computer vision, and acoustic AI, the underlying deep neural network topologies, the difficulty of assaults, and the perceptibility of attacks by humans are all examined. We deployed recent encryption standards to protect patient data transport and storage. Various studies and use cases reveal gains in data security, system reliability, and user trust, with findings indicating increased operational efficiency, decreased errors, and high compliance with regulatory regulations. These results show that our systems can considerably improve the security and efficiency of AI-powered digital health services.

articleTitle: A Review study on Utilizing Deep Learning in Arabic Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Arabic text classification has been revolutionized by deep learning, which provides more efficient techniques for managing the complexity of the language, including rich morphology, diacritical marks, and various dialects. This review highlights the benefits of deep learning models over conventional machine learning methods by examining a variety of models, such as CNNs, RNNs, and transformers like AraBERT.

articleTitle: Enhancing Printed Document Security with QR Code-Based Digital Signatures
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: this paper discusses a new methodology in integrating digital signatures into printed documents using QR code technology. The proposed system will allow users to securely sign documents by creating a unique hash of the document content, encrypting it with the user password, and encoding it into a QR code that would be printed with the document for easy verification of its authenticity and integrity. It includes scanning of documents, re-application of password by the user, and ensuring that the document is not tampered with by matching the validation hash with the hash scanned from the QR Code. An even better way of trying to bring security to the printed documents-just a straightforward yet effective way of validating digital signatures on physical media.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Framework for Efficient and Secure E-Certification Sharing and Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: It is against this backdrop of the cumbersome and time-consuming process of academic certificate validation in Palestine that we proffer an innovative blockchain-based solution. Automation of certificate creation and verification is supported through our system to reduce manual effort and associated costs. The universities upload certificates and data that get hashed on the blockchain. Verification is supported with QR codes, while cryptographic hashing assures authenticity of data. The proposed blockchain framework therefore guarantees ownership control, transparency, and speed for quick processing. This has been empirically proven to be efficient and superior to conventional techniques of evaluation. The proposed system also subscribes to sustainability objectives, since there will be a huge reduction in the use of paper. In this work, we realize a blockchain-based novel framework for issuance and verification of student certifications with integrity of data, ownership control, and less processing time. Our work proposes a game-changing approach that capitalizes on blockchain's inherent features to upgrade certification processes, reduce bureaucracy, and help preserve the environment.

articleTitle: Fingerprint Authentication Method using Two Steps Verification Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper presents a new Fingerprint Authentication method based on a steps verification algorithm. The first verification step depends on feature extraction of contours, edges, and lines in both the source fingerprint image and the stored database images, followed by matching the same edges and lines by measuring the Euclidean distance between pixels of the matched lines. This step indicates realization and recognition between the source fingerprint image and its matched corresponding image in database images. The second verification step is performed to give a final decision of recognition using mutual information as a similarity measure between the source fingerprint image and its initially matched image in database images.The experimental results proved that the proposed fingerprint authentication method gives an accurate and high recognition rate.

articleTitle: VSK - A Tripartite Development Model based on the V-Model, the Scrum, and the Kanban Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Hybrid software development models are increasingly being used in various industries to provide the benefits of agile methodologies in software development while maintaining traditional model frameworks that the rest of the organization may still be utilizing. This paper presents a new tripartite software model (VSK) that has integrated agile methodologies, the Scrum and the Kanban methodologies, along with the traditional methodology the V-model. Since the V-model is commonly used in the automotive space for systems engineering activities, this was selected as the traditional framework for this new tripartite model. The bottom of the V will contain two separate Agile development methodologies that will run in parallel. A scrum methodology will be utilized for new feature development and release planning activities. In parallel to the scrum methodology a Kanban methodology will be used to track bugs and performance issues.

articleTitle: Retinal Blood Vessels Segmentation Using Classical Edge Detection Filters and the Watershed
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Eye diseases are among the leading health risks people face today, with retinal blood vessel extraction being a crucial step in analyzing retinal images for medical diagnoses. The structures and geometric features of retinal blood vessels offer valuable insights into a patient's health and contribute to the diagnosis of conditions of eye diseases in addition to human body diseases such as diabetes and high blood pressure. The goal of all researchers is to prevent blindness by accurate diagnosis and timely treatment of these diseases. In this paper, we suggested an approach for extracting retinal blood vessels that consists of five stages. The first stage involves preprocessing, where the green channel of the input color image is selected, and edges are detected. In the second stage, we label all connected regions, close gaps, and fill holes. The third stage focuses on improving image contrast, applying a Gaussian filter, and using mathematical morphology to highlight the vessel network. The fourth stage involves segmenting the image into several regions using mathematical morphology and the watershed algorithm. Finally, in the fifth stage, small areas not belonging to blood vessels are removed based on their area and perimeter. Experimental results proved that the suggested approach produces a high-quality map of potential blood vessels. The performance metrics confirm the efficiency and accuracy of our approach.

articleTitle: Security Risk Assessment of Humanoid Robotics: DARWIN-OP2 as Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper presents a security risk assessment of a humanoid robot, DARWIN-OP2, controlled through the Robot Operating System (ROS). The assessment utilizes the Cyber Kill Chain framework and focuses on an identified vulnerability: CVE-2011-2523. To exploit this vulnerability, several attack scenarios were studied and analyzed, with the Unauthorized Access Attack type ultimately selected. The aim of these attacks was to gain unauthorized access to the robot’s control system. By exploiting vulnerabilities in the robot’s system, an attacker could potentially obtain sensitive information or establish persistent control over the robot. A qualitative assessment of this scenario revealed that it could successfully compromise the robot, impacting its availability and integrity. This was demonstrated by successfully establishing a reverse shell on the robot. These findings highlight the importance of implementing robust security measures for humanoid robots to mitigate potential risks and ensure their safe and reliable operation.

articleTitle: Hybrid Diabetes Mellitus Prediction Modeling and Analysis Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Diabetes happens when your body fails to manage the portions of the foods you take to convert them to energy. Diabetes, therefore, needs to be detected and treated early well in advance so that health complications may be averted. More recently with the methods of machine learning in place, diabetes can be better predicted. This research will propose a novel approach to a patient‘s diabetes risk level based on a combination of the traditional clinical and the newly proposed HL7 insurance profile. The specific algorithms evaluated and compared are random forest, logistic regression, and ensemble of the two approaches, which when combined, would improve upon the current state-of-the-art methods for the prediction of diabetes risk. In this work, model was evaluated on benchmark datasets containing 15 attributes and the performance was evaluated using the ‘n-fold cross validation‘. For training purposes, the data base was developed using 1500 healthy people from the general population selected at random. The hybrid model has been evaluated with LightGBM. The accuracy of the hybrid model with the LightGBM is 76% for the collected dataset, and 90% for the Pima Data set when applying the problem instances attributes.

articleTitle: A New ECG Denoising Technique based on WATV and Convex Fused-Lasso
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The Electrocardiogram (ECG) signal serves an important role in identifying heart problems, but it is usually distorted by noise, preventing accurate interpretation. Many ECG denoising techniques were proposed in literature. In this paper, a new ECG denoising approach is proposed. It is based on Convex fused lasso Denoising with non-convex regularization and Wavelet/Total Variation (WATV). The performance of this proposed approach is proved by the results obtained from the computations of SNR (Signal to Noise Ratio), the PSNR (Peack SNR), the MSE (Mean Square Error), the Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the Cross-Correlation (CC). These results are obtained by applying this proposed approach and other three denoising techniques. The latters are WATV based denoising technique, Convex fused lasso denoising with non-convex regularization, and a statistical approach to signal denoising based on data-driven multiscale representation. These results show that the proposed denoising approach outperforms the other three mentioned techniques.

articleTitle: Unraveling the 'Safe Harbor ': A Crucial Balance between Liability and Expression in Social Media Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper embarks on a captivating exploration of the 'safe harbor' concept, a pivotal aspect of social media network service provider liability. It delves into the intricate landscape of legal regulation, striving to find a delicate equilibrium between the imperative to safeguard against harm from social network misuse and the fundamental right to expression. The implications are profound: if service providers are held liable for such harms, they may impose stringent posting restrictions, potentially infringing on the right of expression. Conversely, they may lift these restrictions if not held liable, potentially exposing public and private interests to harm. This paper seeks to address this issue by defining safe harbor, its legal basis, its scope, the conditions for its application, our opinion on it, and finally, the most critical results reached.

articleTitle: Enhancing Convergence Efficiency in Federated Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study evaluates federated learning models' performance compared to centralized models using the MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets. Four models were tested: two Federated Learning models and two centralized models. The evaluation focused on accuracy, training rounds, and CO2 emissions, to optimize convergence and reducing energy consumption while maintaining strong model performance. The results showed that Federated learning models outperformed centralized models, with the Federated Learning MNIST model achieving 98.79% accuracy compared to 87.93% for the centralized model. Also, the accuracy of the Federated Learning CIFAR-10 model achieved 91.20% accuracy, exceeding the centralized model’s 90.14%. The most accuracy improvements happened in the early training rounds. An adjusted hill-climbing technique was used to the centralized models, decreasing the number of iterations and CO2 emissions without significantly reducing accuracy.

articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Tools on the Quality of Financial Reports in Service Companies
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study aimed to demonstrate the impact of artificial intelligence tools, represented by (expert systems, and neural networks) on the quality of financial reports in service companies listed on the Amman Stock Exchange. To achieve the objectives of this study, two methodologies were relied upon: The descriptive analytical approach through developing a questionnaire to collect primary data for measuring the elements of the independent variable related to artificial intelligence tools, and the applied approach to estimate the dependent variable represented in the quality of financial reports by relying on the financial statements of service companies listed on the Amman Stock Exchange for the year (2023). Appropriate statistical methods were used to analyze the data and test hypotheses through multiple regression analysis. The results of this study show a positive and strong impact with different values from a statistical perspective of artificial intelligence tools on the quality of financial reports in service companies listed on the Amman Stock Exchange. The expert systems variable came first in terms of strength of impact on achieving quality of financial reports, followed by the neural network’s variable. These results call on those in charge of service companies to increase the use of artificial intelligence tools and urge companies to apply them effectively and give a greater role to information technology experts and smart applications to ensure the efficient and economical application of artificial intelligence tools to increase the quality of produced financial reports, establishing transparency and rising investor confidence in them, and ensuring the efficiency of operations in these companies and supporting their profit continuity.

articleTitle: Hybrid ResNet-ViT Model for Lung Cancer Classification from Histopathology Images
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning model that classifies lung cancer from histopathological images using Residual Networks (ResNet) and Vision Transformers (ViTs). The model uses ResNet for local feature extraction and ViT for global dependencies on the LC25000 dataset, which contains images of adenocarcinoma, benign tissue, and squamous cell carcinoma. The model achieved 99.31% classification accuracy after 10 epochs of training. Diagnostic precision and recall improved significantly, suggesting real-time clinical uses. Future work will explore model optimization, the inclusion of more lung disorders, and the development of multimodal data systems to further enhance diagnostic performance.

articleTitle: Intelligent System for Classifying of Acoustic Endoscopic Images of the Pancreas Based the Analysis of Walsh Spectra of Local Windows
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The purpose of the work is to develop and study methods and algorithms for intelligent classification systems for digital medical images. A method for automatic classification of medical images was developed using neural networks and transparency masks obtained by preliminary image segmentation. This allows you to generate descriptors only for those pixels that are selected by the transparency mask. Also algorithmic and software for classifying medical images has been developed. Experimental testing was carried out on ultrasound images of the pancreas. Differential diagnostics was carried out on control samples. The classes "oncology" and "pancreatitis" were divided. The diagnostic sensitivity by class turned out to be at least 0.8, while the diagnostic specificity is at least 0.85.

articleTitle: ESG Risk Management, Sustainability-Oriented Firms and Financial Distress in the Financial Industry: an AI-aided approach
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study aims to explore the association between the level of ESG risk management in the financial industry and the odds of financial distress. We use a sample of 6160 firm-year observations from 2010-2019 of companies in the financial industry (including Banks, Insurance companies, diversified financials and other financial institutions) from 21 countries. An AI was utilized to generate the financial failure scores. A panel regression with random effects was utilized. A negative association between the level of risk management and the odds of bankruptcy. We observe a positive association between the sustainability strategy scores and the z-values, indicating lower odds of bankruptcy. This study contributes by bringing international evidence of the risk management-financial distress influx. It practically implies that management financial of companies can mitigate their financial instabilities through higher ESG risk management, including green loans, sustainability-linked loans and other climate financing; thereby safeguarding against any potential international fluctuations in global markets.

articleTitle: Real-time vehicle detection and classification using deep-transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Nowadays, vision systems are increasingly present in the road context, particularly in surveillance cameras. These systems help ensure safety, monitor traffic, detect congestion, and facilitate mobility. To optimize the performance of these vision systems, it is necessary to have a reliable detection and classification system. Following the great success of convolutional neural networks, we proposed a machine learning-based road images classification approach, using transfer learning, to address the problem of vehicle detection and classification and provide real-time traffic statistics. In this work, the detection and classification of vehicles have been performed using various deep neural network algorithms, including Faster R-CNN, ResNet, YOLO, SSD, and VGG16. The method can differentiate between five classes: bicycle, motorbike, car, bus, and truck.The deep learning method’s training and testing phases were carried out using a database composed of images captured from videos recorded by ADM Morocco, as well as images from GitHub, Kaggle, and the database called CEREMA. Obtained results reached a classification accuracy of 83. 54% using YOLO. For models based on Faster R-CNN for detection, classification with ResNet reached 90. 15% accuracy, while using VGG resulted in 90. 14%. Similarly, SSD models combined with VGG and ResNet both obtained an accuracy of 87. 73%. The best performance was achieved by combining Faster R-CNN and SSD for detection, followed by ResNet for classification, which yielded an accuracy of 90. 31%.

articleTitle: A Proposed Approach for Risk Planning and Management
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Project Risk management is the process of identifying, evaluating, avoiding, or reducing risks. Where there is no software project without risks existence are natural in the context of project planning and management. This study focuses on proposing an enhanced risk management approach where testing phases were added to make the risk management process more effective by proposing solutions to many mistakes and challenges that occur through dealing with risks. The proposed approach focuses on dealing with risks that cannot be easily defined, more accurate risk evaluation, planning, and managing risk coordinated with a contingency plan.

articleTitle: Investigates the Impact of AI-generated Code Tools on Software Readability Code Quality Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has made great strides in various industries, including software development, with tools such as ChatGPT changing the way code is written, maintained and developed. This study investigates the impact of AI-generated code on software quality, focusing on readability, code clarity, complexity, and documentation. Comparing AI-generated code with open-source code from GitHub for three tasks of varying difficulty (easy, medium, and hard), we evaluated key metrics such as cyclomatic complexity (CC), code lines, comment density, code-to-code ratio, and variable names. The results revealed that although both AI-generated and human-generated code can be concise and efficient, code generated by AI tools shows a greater focus on documentation more clearly. AI-generated code especially in complex tasks showed improved readability due to higher comment density and the use of clear variable names. These results show that AI tools such as ChatGPT can enhance code quality, especially in the software industry where readability and comprehensibility are critical.

articleTitle: Simulating a Finite-State Markov Chain for Rayleigh Block-Fading Channel based on its Mathematical Model, and Practical Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: In the proposed paper, simulating the Finite State Markov Chain (FSMC) to be implemented as Rayleigh Block-fading channel. Indeed, FSMC is regarded as a practical fading channel because of its random choice for future transmission probability. Accordingly, this paper introduces the FSMC technology with the theoretical limits and equations; moreover, the uplink and downlink Rayleigh Block-fading channel scenarios are also investigated and supported by the simulation set-up. The results for the Rayleigh fading channel for the Long-Term Evaluation-Advanced network were obtained as an example of the channel's attitude. The findings demonstrate that FSMC provides such reliable results and is suitable for use as a practical fading channel, particularly in terms of burst error behavior.

articleTitle: Enhanced Arabic Feature Selection using an Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Research in the field of Natural Language Processing for Arabic documents that incorporate metaheuristic techniques remain limited, primarily due to the intricate nature of the language, which encompasses challenges related to its structure, morphology, syntactic analysis, grammatical conventions, and derivational processes. This study introduces a novel approach for the processing of Arabic documents, which aims to enhance the whale optimization algorithm. This approach functions as a supervised learning technique, emulating the behaviors of whales, including bubble netting and spiral movements toward their targets. The proposed methodology represents an advancement of the traditional whale optimization algorithm, characterized by its adaptability and efficiency. It effectively integrates exploration and exploitation strategies, drawing inspiration from the natural behaviours of humpback whales while also incorporating the beneficial attributes of chaotic functions. This adaptability positions the method to address complex optimization challenges across various fields. Beside, the experiment show that enhanced method has a better result by using Firefly Algorithm classifier and the TF-IDFC-RF feature extraction.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study between Agile and Waterfall Methodologies during Software Development Process
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study aims to investigate and compare the using of waterfall and agile methodologies in the software development process. A survey were collected from 2017 to 2023 to investigate the use of waterfall and agile methodologies in software development. Moreover, the papers were classified based on published year, country, and used software development methods. In addition, the papers were summarized to highlight the state of the art of the most research investigate to comparison of using a waterfall and agile development processes. The research result discover that agile has shown the best results compared to other techniques for big software project furthermore agile requires small team members, also it shows acceptable result on small to medium projects, is more flexible to requirements changes, and software testing can be implemented after each sprint. The research result shows that waterfall methodology for small to medium projects is acceptable for small team.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Higher Education: Predicting and Mitigating Student Dropout
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to address the challenge of student attrition in higher education institutions by developing an early warning system (EWS) using machine learning algorithms. A combination of Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models was employed to predict student dropout rates. A dataset of 12,220 students, including enrollment information, financial standing, and academic indicators, was utilized. Data preprocessing involved handling missing values and feature engineering. The Random Forest model achieved the highest accuracy at 93%, followed by the Decision Tree at 91% and the Support Vector Machine at 89%. Feature importance analysis identified key predictors of attrition, such as Current Earned Hours, Overall CGPA, and financial standing. The findings suggest that targeted interventions and support strategies can improve student retention. The study highlights the potential of machine learning techniques in predicting student attrition and providing actionable insights for effective interventions. The cross-validation process ensured the reliability and generalizability of the models, contributing valuable knowledge to the field of educational data analytics.

articleTitle: Predicting Students’ Performance using Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper presents students’ performance prediction model based on Machine Learning (ML) classifiers. The used dataset provides three groups of features that may affect students’ performance. Features selection approaches have been applied to the dataset. Several well-known ML classifiers including Neural Network (ANN), Bayes Network (Bayes Net), and Decision Tree (DT). Along with the original approach, hyper approach is applied using boosting, bagging, and voting classifiers. The performance of these algorithms is examined and compared using a confusion matrix. Results show that behavioral features have a major impact on students’ performance and ML algorithms can be used effectively to build students’ performance prediction model.

articleTitle: Smart Logistics Services: How Artificial Intelligence Transforms Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The aims of this research are to explore the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in logistics decision-making processes and to address the challenges faced by logistics managers, such as increasing supply chain complexity and the need for precise, real-time decision-making. The research analyses primary AI use-cases in logistics, including predictive analytics for demand and disruption predictions, optimization algorithms fil route and warehouse efficiency, as well as autonomous systems for operational automation. Together, these technologies enable greater precision in decision-making and operational agility and efficiency. Further, the study examines how AI is disrupting supply chain visibility and risk management proficiencies with instant data processing, better hazard control, as well as a refined risk mitigation process. AI has been realized into process and the outcome was noteworthy in comparison of manual work procedures and allows mangers make strategic decisions since it creates automation. The results reinforce how utilizing AI does not only enhance logistics but also helps to increase the transparency of and boost the resilience of competition in the whole supply chain. The findings of this study offer useful implications for logistics management to effectively implement AI in order to innovate regular logistical decision-making, and make the over-all supply chain more agile & efficient.

articleTitle: Civil Liability of The Data Controller For Data Storage: A General Perspective In Light of The UAE Personal Data Protection Law
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study analyzes the civil liability of the data controller concerning data storage and the administration of personal information. It specifically addresses the responsibilities of the data controller for the processing of personal data, emphasizing the data owner's right to request the deletion of their personal information. In the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the legal framework for personal data protection has significantly evolved, particularly with the enactment of Federal Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data. This legislation delineates the obligations of data controllers, particularly in instances of noncompliance with legal mandates for data deletion. The paper examines the responsibilities of the data controller in protecting personal data, highlighting the conditions necessitating data deletion and the legal obligations that ensue when these conditions are not fulfilled. It further examines the type and scope of legal liability that may be imposed on data controllers for non-compliance with data protection legislation, including potential compensation for losses suffered by the data owner. This paper examines pertinent legal provisions and judicial interpretations in the UAE to elucidate the data controller's responsibilities in personal data protection and the legal ramifications of non-compliance with these obligations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Steganography in Formats of Digital Images
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Steganography is a technique used for embedding information within digital files. The main goal of steganography is to send secret data inside another object without any suspicion of its existence. It is the art of hiding information. Hackers use steganography to contain malware to avoid easy identification by the various security measures. Embedded information should not be noticed in any way. This paper uses LSB to compare the result of embedding messages inside the Metadata of different digital image formats BMP, JPG, PNG, and TIFF. Metadata is the information explains the file’s content. Different measures were used for evaluation process MSE, PSNR, SSIM, and the histogram.

articleTitle: Solar Panel Soiling Classification Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of solar panels as a sustainable and cost-effective source of energy, it becomes paramount to ensure that these panels perform well, especially that they are prone to several factors that can affect their performance. One of these factors is soiling and dusting. This research agrees with other related studies confirming that machine learning methods are useful in PV systems monitoring. This paper aims at researching the application of machine learning algorithms to identify the soiled panels. In particular, the paper investigates the ability of the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Time Large Language Model (LLM) Transformer machine learning algorithms to detect and classify soiling on photovoltaic panels, thus notifying the responsible person to do the needed cleaning. Both models were trained on the time-series data that were collected by the researchers, including: the temperature, humidity, and irradiance. The models’ performances were ana-lyzed with the help of evaluation metrics. The highest accuracy of the LSTM model in the identifications of soiling patterns was up to 96.11%, whereas in the Time LLM Transformer model was 93.6%.

articleTitle: Navigating Artificial Intelligence in Strategic Management in Schools and Organizations
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study logically discusses navigating artificial intelligence (AI) in strategic management in schools and organizations. It identified AI innovations in strategic management, including generative adversarial networks, natural language processing, predicting analysis, and reinforcement learning. The study outlined AI implications for strategic management and discussed the essentials of AI in strategic management. Meanwhile, navigating AI in strategic management can be done through these approaches such as defining the objectives, developing a strategy, personnel training, developing a pilot project, and conducting evaluation and performance appraisal on the integrating processes. However, this study discusses the challenges of AI in strategic management integration and outlines the solutions to the challenges of integrating AI into the strategic management of schools and organizations. This study concluded that Navigating AI into strategic management enhances the school and organization to be more data-driven, adaptive, and efficient in-service delivery with improved productivity.

articleTitle: The power of Network Penetration Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: In this paper, a review of penetration tests and their power is conducted to give a holistic understanding of the secure network. Furthermore, this paper introduces a full knowledge of the tester methods and the performance and the point of strengths, the weaknesses, and how we understand the process and proceed for testing or securing your network.

articleTitle: Theft Alarm and Notification System for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Local security within a building or work area for supplies such as medical storage rooms or tool cribs is paramount for safety and inventory cost. This paper presents a design which seeks to implement a self-operating general purpose and medical supply security system. This consists of sensors and LEDs connected to a TI (Texas Instruments) TIVA C Series TM4C123GH6PM microcontroller. This paper presents a unique security system in that instead of an implementation across an entire house or building it can be specially configured for smaller scale use cases such as storage containers or rooms. The design is modular and can be integrated with lights and control actuators that take a digital input signal as a control input. The proposed design follows a software engineering method of development and performed testing to prove the requirements are met and show the real time features of the system.

articleTitle: Maximize Leader Election Algorithm Performance in Bi-Directional Ring Networks With Both Links Down Between Two Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The process of selecting a leader to avoid instability in distributed system network after leader failure is called Leader Election Algorithm (LEA). This process becomes more complicated when it faces intermittent or complete links disconnected. the network becomes a one-way behavior if both lines of communication between two points are disrupted and thus the network becomes very slow, especially in systems where time is a critical issue, and the process of communication between points becomes much slower if the network leader is next to the fault or close to it, so the criteria will be established to ensures that the system leader in the Bidirectional ring communication network is in a place that allows next leader to communicate with all points as quickly as possible, and this will be during the election operation.This research presents a solution for leader failure problem in bidirectional ring network. This research takes into account the existence of intermittent or disconnection links between nodes. It will produce three algorithms to determine a new leader in the network with maximum network performance. It uses the least probability of time steps and the number of messages needed to elect the new leader in bidirectional ring network with N communicated nodes. so that the system remains able to work and communicate with its best capacity during this problem with the number of message complexity O(N) in the worst case. The third scenario minimizes the value of proper leader ID $\frac{{I{D_{Current}}}}{{{I_{Current}}idStepCount}}$, and maximizes the value of proper leader place N − (N − nStepCount).

articleTitle: Real-Time VPN Anomaly Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper implements a network traffic analysis system with a focus on cybersecurity applications. The novelty lies in its combined approach of real-time traffic monitoring and machine learning-driven anomaly detection. Using the Scapy library, the core system extracts features such as packet rates, inter-arrival times, port usage, and TTL distributions from live network traffic. Four classifiers were evaluated for their effectiveness in detecting potential threats or unusual patterns, such as VPN usage. The Random Forest classifier achieved the highest accuracy at (0.976), followed by Gradient Boosting with an accuracy of (0.967). Logistic Regression demonstrated an accuracy of (0.902), while the Support Vector Machine (SVM) recorded a lower accuracy of (0.694). These results underscore the system’s potential to accurately identify network anomalies, making it a valuable tool for cybersecurity professionals.

articleTitle: From Monochrome to Technicolor: A Comprehensive Review of Video Colorization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Video colorization is the process of adding colors to black and white video. This task is a compelling problem and intriguing challenge in image processing. With the emergence of deep learning and the availability of a wide range of datasets, significant developments have been made in video colorization algorithms. However, this task presents unique challenges, particularly in ensuring temporal coherence and maintaining spatiotemporal consistency across frames. In this work, we aim to offer a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art techniques in video colorization, examining the challenges, progress in current techniques, and future direction, by analyzing many papers and research. The goal of this paper is to provide the researchers with a piece of valuable information about video colorization.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Early Detection of Heart Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The main objective of the study is to predict the probability of developing heart disease using a Decision Tree Classifier, K-nearest neighbors, and Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression. Age, sexual pressure, quantity, and levels are among the variables included in the Kaggle dataset. A combination of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity was used to train and evaluate the algorithms. Based on the accuracy of participants' predictions, the results suggest that learning algorithms could help treat heart disease.The "Heart Disease Prediction"project contains all project information and results. Contributing to the use of multiple algorithms improves patient outcomes to enhance the detection and treatment of heart diseases. Logistic Regression has achieved an accuracy of 86.41%. A module capable of predicting heart disease in a patient has been implemented. A variety of techniques are employed to assess models, including F-measure, ROC, precision, recall, and accuracy. The bagging set learning method using logistic regression provides the best performance, according to the data.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Two-Stage Tiny Bootloader for Flash-Constrained Microcontrollers Using RAM Execution
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative two-stage Tiny Bootloader (TBL) that primarily runs in Random Access Memory (RAM), reducing reliance on Flash memory. In contrast to conventional bootloaders, which are stored mostly in Flash, this design optimizes Flash usage, which is particularly advantageous for microcontrollers with limited Flash capacity. By relocating most of the bootloader code to RAM, the proposed approach frees up Flash memory for program data, making it highly suitable for resource-constrained embedded systems. The implementation is showcased using the STM32G031K4 microcontroller with Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART) communication. This paper will go over the concept, design, implementation, and testing of the new proposed Tiny Bootloader.

articleTitle: Social Media Transparency: How Digital Marketing Shapes Strategic Decisions
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This research seeks to clarify the effect of digital marketing during the decision-making process regarding the social media atmosphere, studying such influences and transparency as mediating factors in Jordan. A structured questionnaire was used as a tool for developing the primary data amongst active users of different social media platforms. We used the PLS-SEM technique in this research to examine associations among digital marketing effectiveness, transparency and decision-making constructs. Transparency influences important factors of the decision-making process guided by digital marketing, according to this study. The enhanced transparency, in turn, improved consumer trust and satisfaction, leading to better-informed decision-making. In addition, the transparency of marketing messages due to social media dynamics leads to more involved consumer involvement. The results emphasize the importance of digital marketers being transparent in their operations as part of designing future-proof consumer trust and competitive differentiation. Theoretical Implications, which contribute to the literature by • Providing empirical evidence of transparency as a mediator in the relationship between digital marketing and decision-making; Practical Implications for Marketers and Policymakers, to inform marketers and policymakers aiming to encourage consumer trust through more transparent social media interactions.

articleTitle: Deepfake Video Detection: Analysis for Deep Learning models using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The unchecked spread of deepfake videos jeopardizes public trust, national security, and media credibility. The capacity to recognize falsified videos is critical for protecting privacy and combatting misinformation. The article seeks to illustrate the usage of Deep Learning (DL) approaches for recognizing deepfake videos, including Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and an RNN-LSTM combination with Transfer Learning. The research used the LSTM model to examine the efficacy of temporal correlations between video frames in the Deepfake Detection Challenge (DFDC) dataset of deep fake videos, and it claimed complete success in both the training and testing stages. In addition, the study used frame level masks and characteristics that were created throughout the research's pre-processing steps. The findings show that the model had a train loss of 0.021 and a test loss of 0.813, suggesting that it was extremely resilient. Other crucial indicator measures, such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), aid in evaluating the model's performance and validate its high accuracy in recognizing deepfake material. This study is very important since it greatly contributes to the body of knowledge in the early phases of deepfake identification and aids in the mitigation of the risks connected with manipulated media.

Author Keywords: Long Short-Term Memory and Recurrent Nural Networks

articleTitle: Analyzing Chaotic Jerk System with Hyperbolic Sine: a new algorithm for Engineering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: this paper examines numerical solutions and applications of an innovative Chaotic Jerk System utilizing the Caputo-Fabrizio fractional derivative (CF-FD). Chaotic systems display complex and unpredictable behaviors, which are recognized as significant in secure communication, data encryption, and random number generation. Employing both the Caputo-Fabrizio fractional derivative and the theory of fractional calculus allows this study to present complex behaviors in compliance with memory effects and long-range interdependence. The computational approach has been introduced in the work and used to solve this chaotic system, which will eventually help us explore the dynamic behavior of such systems. At the same time, it scrutinizes a system's chaos, although closely recreating its action with. Initial conditions and parameters by executing numerical analysis, for example. Moreover, the paper gives an illustrative example for using this chaotic system in secure communication, data encryption, and random number generation. This article develops the phase form of a four-dimensional chaotic system using fractional calculus techniques and, hence, manipulates its chaos. The study provides a bridge between theory and application, an important function that allows for modern innovations in a wide spectrum of areas. We quantified the behavior of this system through numerical simulations and analytical exams, addressing methodologically different conditions thereon. These goals feed into a deeper knowledge of emergent complex chaotic dynamics as well as how the system might be implemented in applications such as secure communication and data encryption. Fractional calculus and chaotic systems have numerous and ever-expanding applications in engineering, helping to improve signal processing, modeling, communication, control, encryption, and our general knowledge of complicated dynamic systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Parameter Tuning with Double Layer Genetic Algorithm for Solving TSP
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: To address the issue of genetic algorithm (GA) performance heavily relying on parameter selection, this paper introduces a double-layer loop adaptive parameter tuning mechanism. This mechanism integrates the concept of GA as a meta-optimizer with adaptive GA, forming a nested two-layer GA structure. The outer GA, acting as the meta-optimizer, evaluates and adjusts the hyperparameters of the inner GA based on individual fitness changes. The inner adaptive GA solves the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) through genetic operations. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly enhances the algorithm's performance and efficiency by dynamically adjusting key parameters. Compared to traditional optimization algorithms, the proposed adaptive parameter tuning mechanism exhibits superior efficiency and stability in solving TSP.

articleTitle: An Overview of Tools and Techniques in Network Forensics
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Network forensics pertains to a subfield of digital forensics that deals with network security. It is utilized in conjunction with computer network traffic monitoring and analysis, which acts as an intrusion detection system and firewall and facilitates the collection of data and digital proof for network security. This platform is designed to analyze and monitor data in a real-time network environment. It is a crucial instrument for identifying and resolving instances of real-time network misuse. This research shows the differences between network forensics and digital forensics as well as the tools and techniques used in network forensics. It also discusses building forensics platforms, developing network analysis methodologies, and talking about the future of network forensics.

articleTitle: Innovative Machine Learning Solutions for Automated Kidney Tumor Detection in CT Imaging Through Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The most common urinary system cancer is kidney cancer, the 7th leading cause of cancers death in men and women worldwide. The early and prompt diagnosis of renal cancer is very important for the survival rate in patients. In this work we provide a study concerning whether machine learning techniques—specifically Random Forest (RF) and Neural Networks (NN)—could be helpful for the computer-aided diagnosis of kidney tumors in CT images. Both models were trained and tested on a dataset from Kagglewhich contain 10000 CT scans, the set is balanced between normal (5000 image) & tumor type of tumors case images. The results indicate that the NN model have higher accuracies than those of RF, 99% versus 98%. Moreover, in all evaluation measures like precision score and recall values F1-score etc, this NN model improved so that it could be treated as a more accurate tool for diagnosis. The automated method minimises the time taken to diagnose and lightens radiologists' load, aiding a timely discovery of cancer at an early stage. The research indicates that adding machine learning tools to clinical practice would allow us to improve the speed and accuracy of diagnosing kidney tumors, with potential benefits for patient care and survival. In the future, bettering these models and studying on larger samples with more diversity are hoped to be achieved.

articleTitle: Controlling DC Motor Speed with FoPID-Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This work aims to propose several designs for controlling the direct-current motor (or simply DC motor) speed. Such motor is broadly used in numerous applications like blowers, lathe machines, cranes, elevators, milling machines, fans, drilling rigs, etc. To achieve our aim, the DC motor model will be first fractionalized and then the so-called Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm will be executed to adjust the proposed controllers’ parameters. This actually would be performed to the resultant fractional-order transfer function. Accordingly, several Fractional-order PID controllers (FoPID-controllers) will be formulated in agreement with the Outstaloup approach, which is typically used to approximate the yielded Laplacian operators s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">±α</sup>, where 0 < α < 1. The controllers generated in accordance with different values of fractional-order values will be then competed to each other to outline which of them has an ability to provide to the closed-loop system of the DC motor speed model a minimal overshoot, short settling time and short rise time.

articleTitle: Feature Selection for Geomagnetic Storm Forecasting Using Particle Swarm Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Geomagnetic activity is a significant research area due to its impact on navigation, satellites, and other technologies. The geomagnetic index Kp is particularly essential for monitoring such activity. Forecasting geomagnetic storms can provide early warnings, helping to mitigate potential disasters. Various methods, including empirical models, physics-based models, and machine learning models, are employed for forecasting. This study focuses on Machine learning models, emphasising selecting appropriate features to enhance prediction accuracy. The primary aim was to improve the 3-hour Kp predictions compared to prior research. Model performance was primarily evaluated using the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> metric. Additionally, RMSE was calculated to ensure comparability with studies that did not use R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The model’s ability to detect storms was assessed by classifying results as Kp>5 (storm) or Kp<5 (not a storm), with the F1 score used as the evaluation metric for classification. The best model achieved an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.71, an RMSE of 0.6671, and an F1 score of 0.6.

articleTitle: Ethical Considerations in AI-Driven HCI Systems in Software Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) systems has transformed user inter-actions with technology, offering unprecedented personalisation and efficiency. However, these advances also raise substantial ethical concerns that need careful consideration, especially from a software engineering perspective. This paper explores AI-driven HCI systems’ ethical challenges, including privacy, bias, transparency, user autonomy, and accountability. We review existing literature to outline the current state of ethical practices and identify significant gaps. Subsequently, we propose a comprehensive framework for addressing these ethical challenges throughout the software development lifecycle. Through this exploration, we highlight the importance of embedding ethical considerations in designing, implementing, and maintaining AI-driven systems, ensuring that these technologies are influential and trustworthy. The discussion is enriched with practical examples and a case study that illustrates the application of these principles in real-world scenarios. This paper seeks to contribute to the ongoing discourse on ethical AI in HCI, urging a proactive approach to developing ethically-aware software solutions.

articleTitle: Blockchain's Role in Emerging Markets: Accelerating Digital Supply Chain Management and Unlocking New Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The This research investigates the influence of blockchain on digital supply chain management in volatile nodes-on-stake markets. This research focuses on the functionality of blockchain in streamlining supply chain operations with an insight into its adoption and implementation in untapped industries. Findings are based on interviews and case studies conducted with companies implementing blockchain within their supply chains using a qualitative approach for data collection. The key results reveal that blockchain can help improve traceability, decrease operation costs and potentially unlock new business opportunities. The report uncovers and addresses blockchain's advantages and disadvantages and future concerns with the technology while offering advice for those looking to begin their own digital operations using enterprise-level blockchain.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Embedded Alcohol Detection System for Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The threat of driving under the influence of "unreasonable" drinking is responsible for more than 60% of the increasing number of accidents in the world. This paper presents an embedded system for detecting alcohol. In this paper a self-testing breathalyzer will be designed so that drivers can better avoid the danger of drunk driving. The proposed model was created using a PC connected with the Arduino Mega board, alcohol detection sensors, and other sensors. Alcohol detection sensor (MQ-3) is connected to the Arduino Mega when the driver breathes through to detect the blood alcohol level. Each time the driver exhales, a sensor measures the alcohol level and analyses whether it is within a "safe" range. When excessive alcohol levels are detected, the results are displayed on an OLED screen, and it triggers an alarm (a buzzer and an LED light). The paper also presents a proposal for a global alcohol detection system with Ignition Interlock Devices (IID) capability. We are proposing using a phone as a biometric verification method to detect the Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of the driver, measured using an infrared spectroscopy sensor, and communicate back to a central station system through a vehicle controller.

articleTitle: Multi Label Classification Based on Ensemble Learning: Investigative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: In the big data technology nowadays, activities associated with Multi-Label Classification (MLC) pose big and complex challenges, receiving terrific interest in diverse fields. Existing MLC algorithms suffer from low overall performance. This paper considers four well-known Problem Transformation Methods (PTMs). Two of these PTMs are based on the frequency of the labels (MFL and LFL) while the last two PTMs are based on the positive correlations among labels. These PTMs have been implemented and compared against four multi label datasets of various sizes to identify the best one that fits the nature of MLC datasets. Moreover, six popular ensemble learning models have been carried out and compared on the four datasets with respect to several evaluation metrics such as Accuracy, Hamming loss, and Exact Match and using SMO, DecisionStump, Random Forest, and Random Commission classifiers. The results revealed that MFL accomplished the quality performance amongst the four PTMs, and Stacking SVM is the best ensemble learning technique.

articleTitle: Prediction of Hypertension Disease Using Machine Learning Techniques: Case Study from Jordan
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
