abstract: Hypertension is one of the most common diseases in Jordan. It is one of the main reasons of death among Jordanian adult citizens. Worldwide, nearly 13% of all deaths are due to Hypertension with nearly 8 million deaths yearly. Hence, this research is interested in the early prediction of this disease among Jordanian people. To achieve this main objective, Machine Learning (ML) is utilized through a large number of classification models and considering five well-known evaluation metrics. These classification models have been trained on a primary dataset that has been collected for the purpose of the research. The results revealed that Random Forest, Random Committee, and MultilayerPerceptron are the best classification models to handle the task of the early prediction of Hypertension in Jordan.

articleTitle: Improving WebRTC Quality-of-Service Using SDN and a Load Balancing Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Effective communication is a fundamental element of numerous modern digital technologies. Among protocols, Web Real-Time Communication (WebRTC) has received the most attention. So that, this protocol enables the direct integration of peer-to-peer real-time communication into browsers. Besides, Software-Defined Networking (SDN) is beneficial for WebRTC applications, especially over video communications. This study implements a model called (WRTSDN) based WebRTC through Software -Defined -networking. WRTSDN is a WebRTC and SDN approach for offering the best route from a network-wide perspective. In addition, this work has been achieved and compared using two models, such as (WebRTC without SDN) and (WRTSDN). These models have the same structure and consist of 8 hosts and 20 switches arranged in a fat tree topology. The Network structure has been done in the real world with access, distribution, aggregation, edge, and core routers. To evaluate the performance of both models, four metrics are utilised: round-trip time, jitter, throughput, and delay. The results demonstrate that the WRTSDN method effectively transfers data on the route for a fat-tree topology while satisfying the criterion of lower delay compared to the standard WebRTC protocol. Also, the WRTSDN framework exhibited minimal variation in the jitter metric. This characteristic means that the model is well-suited for applications in real-time that demand consistent and superior quality of service (QoS) performance. Finally, the WRTSDN technique presented a significant result in measuring delay compared to the standard WebRTC protocol.

articleTitle: Student Teachers’ Attitudes towards the Use of ChatGPT in Teaching
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The study aimed at identifying student teachers’ attitudes towards the use of ChatGPT application in teaching in relation to the length of teaching experience, specialism and cumulative GPA. The sample included student teachers on practicum on the Postgraduate Professional Diploma in Teaching Program in the College of Education, Humanities and Social Sciences, Al Ain University, during the first semester of the academic year 2024/2025. The study used a questionnaire of (22) items distributed under three domains, namely: Planning, Implementation and Evaluation.The results of the study showed that the mean scores of student teachers' attitudes in the combined domains were high, with domain of evaluation on top with the highest mean score of (4.06), the domain of planning for teaching was ranked last with a mean score of (4.03). The results showed that there were no statistically significant differences between student teachers’ attitudes towards the use of ChatGPT application based on the cumulative GPA variable. Nonetheless, there were statistically significant differences in these attitudes in terms of the effect of the variable of years of experience, in favor of teachers with long experience. As for the effect of specialism, data revealed that there were statistically significant differences in favor of scientific disciplines.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach Towards Software Regression Testing Quality Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Software testing is very important in software development to ensure its quality and reliability. As software systems have become more complex, the number of test cases has increased, which presents the challenge of executing all the tests in a limited time frame. Various test case prioritization techniques have been introduced to solve this problem. These methods aim to identify and implement the most critical tests first. In this paper, we propose an implementation of a dynamic test case prioritization strategy to improve software quality by increasing code coverage with special attention to edge case handling. Edge case test prioritization is a technique that improves test efficiency by selecting extreme case scenarios that can reveal critical bugs or unexpected behavior early in development, improving overall software reliability and dependability. In order to prioritize test cases, this paper presents a regression-based method that makes use of machine learning algorithms. The approach leverages previous performance data to optimize regression testing efficiency by examining variables like test time and execution status. Performance evaluations, when compared against industry standards and cutting-edge techniques, show how effective these algorithms are at correctly prioritizing test cases and identifying faults. This study offers simplified yet reliable solutions for regression testing optimization by shedding light on the efficacy of regression algorithms, such as Random Forest and decision trees.

articleTitle: IoT-Integrated Cashless Sanitary Pad Vending Machine for Sustainable Menstrual Hygiene Management in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Access to menstrual hygiene products remains a significant challenge for many women in underserved areas, particularly in rural and suburban regions of Bangladesh. A comprehensive survey involving 374 women across urban, suburban, and rural communities revealed that over 30% of respondents in urban and suburban areas still face difficulties accessing feminine care products, with 42% citing lack of availability as a major challenge. To address these issues, this study proposes an IoT-integrated, cashless sanitary pad vending machine designed to improve accessibility. The proposed solution utilizes RFID technology, a mobile payment recharge system (e.g. bKash), and edge computing to enhance user experience, reduce operational costs, and increase convenience. A prototype of the vending machine was developed and tested, demonstrating high reliability in dispensing products and facilitating user transactions. The results indicated a 30% faster dispensing time compared to existing methods, emphasizing significant efficiency gains. Additionally, the comparative analysis highlighted reduced payment time when using registered RFID tags. These findings suggest that IoT and edge computing can play a crucial role in enhancing menstrual product access for underserved populations. Future work includes incorporating AI for predictive inventory management and enhanced data security, supporting sustainable menstrual health solutions in schools, workplaces, and rural communities.

articleTitle: Automatic Diagnosis of Sarcoidosis Stage Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Sarcoidosis is a rare multisystem disease primarily manifesting in the lungs and classified into four stages based on its impact on the lungs. Due to its rarity, sarcoidosis is often misdiagnosed. Data containing chest X-ray images were collected, preprocessed, and segmented to extract Regions of Interest (ROI). Relevant textural features were then extracted using Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix techniques to represent lung tissue efficiently. The collected images were fed into classifiers, including "K Nearest Neighbors," "Support Vector Machine," and "Artificial Neural Network," for training. The classifiers were trained and tested on non-overlapping subsets of the datasets, achieving overall accuracies of 92.03%, 89.13%, and 81.16%, respectively, with the KNN classifier outperforming the others across all metrics.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Dynamic Cooperative Evolution Algorithm for Constrained Multi-objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Compared with multi-objective optimization problems(MOPs), constrained multi-objective optimization problems(CMOPs) have to consider the impact of constraints on seeking Pareto front in addition to convergence and diversity, thus how to balance these factors is a challenging task of CMOPs. To confront this challenge, a new two-stage dynamic collaborative evolutionary algorithm, called TSDCEA, is proposed to solve the CMOPs. TSDCEA divides the evolutionary process of the population into two stages. In the first stage, the two populations evolve collaboratively so that the auxiliary population rapidly explores infeasible regions while the main population explores feasible regions. The auxiliary population stops evolving when it basically reaches the unconstrained pareto front(UPF) and the population evolution process switches to the second stage. Then the main population applies a dynamic ε-constraint method, while the auxiliary population is utilized for differential evolution with elite individuals from the main population. The generated new offspring participate in environmental selection to explore feasible regions close to the main population and encourage the main population to disperse widely in the explored feasible regions. Comparative experiments show that the TSDCEA algorithm is more competitive than other state-of-the-art constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithms(CMOEAs).

articleTitle: Impact of User Innovativeness on Metaverse Adoption
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: the study focuses on the integration of the metaverse to enhance online learning platforms, particularly among Omani students. The research evaluates the acceptance of the metaverse using a conceptual model that emphasizes key adoption properties such as user mobility, users’ accessibility and users’ and ubiquity. The novelty of the paper lies in introducing the users’ innovativeness as a moderator which positively influences other variables. The results indicate a favorable impact of the moderator on the mentioned variables. The practical implication of the study suggests that authorities in Oman should recognize the metaverse's significance as a transformative tool for online learning. Furthermore, managerial implications recommend the implementation of the metaverse in governmental sectors to enhance the learning environment in the Sultanate of Oman.

articleTitle: Correlation-Driven Feature Selection and Penalty-Enhanced Autoencoder for Dimensionality Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: High-dimensional datasets often pose challenges for data mining and machine learning due to redundant and irrelevant information. In this work, a hybrid strategy is proposed that reduces dimensionality while preserving relevant data and minimizing computation time for tasks like classification. The method combines correlation measures with an auto-encoder, improving data processing, storage, and visualization. Initially, the approach selects the most relevant features using correlation, then applies an auto-encoder to further reduce the dataset while preserving nonlinear relationships. A penalty on the reconstruction error is also proposed to maintain correlation between the input and output layers of the auto-encoder. Experiments demonstrate that the method enhances accuracy and reduces dimensionality without losing information, offering a potential advance in dimensionality reduction techniques.

articleTitle: Sustainability in Three Dimensions: Mapping the Metaverse’s Blueprint on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through a Bibliometric Journey
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study explored the role of the metaverse in advancing Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Addressing global challenges such as quality education, health, climate action, and social equity, the study aimed to evaluate how Metaverse applications may enhance or accelerate these SDG goals. This study employed a systematic and bibliometric literature review to examine 63 documents from the Scopus database, which were chosen from an initial pool of 21,095. The study used VOSviewer software to map bibliometric trends and research density across countries, the research level, keywords, types, and roles of the metaverse for SDGs, and the impact of the metaverse on SDGs. The results highlighted Metaverse’s versatility in promoting SDGs. For instance, virtual classrooms support SDG 4 (quality education), enabling global access to education, while virtual workspaces support SDG 13 (climate action), reducing travel-related emissions. However, barriers remain, including technological access disparities, lack of regulation, and potential environmental impact from data centers. The metaverse promises SDG advancement but requires global collaboration and policy development to bridge digital divides and mitigate ecological impact. We need future research to enhance our understanding of practical Metaverse applications and improve governance frameworks.

articleTitle: Leveraging Blockchain for Ethical Sourcing and Sustainability in Supply Chains: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Ethical sourcing and sustainability within supply chains are increasingly acknowledged as key components of modern procurement methodologies. This systematic literature review thoroughly evaluates the current scholarly dialogue regarding blockchain-based strategies that foster ethical sourcing and sustainability within supply chain management (SCM). This study methodically examines academic contributions from 2016 to 2024 to clarify significant trends, obstacles, and prospects related to deploying blockchain technology in enhancing ethical practices and sustainability within supply chains. The findings of this systematic literature review indicate that blockchain operates as a validation tool for organizations attempting to confirm compliance with ethical sourcing standards. Furthermore, the contribution of blockchain to the advancement of sustainability includes its ability to facilitate resource optimization and improve decision-making processes within remanufacturing activities, thereby reinforcing the principles of a circular economy. This study identifies the lack of a practical blockchain framework to be integrated within supply chain management in different industries. It also emphasizes the necessity for empirical research to assess blockchain’s utility in supply chains. This paper reviews blockchain applications in various industries, such as food, Agri-food, and financial flows of humanitarian supply for the enhancement of ethical sourcing, sustainability, and transparency. Major trends, challenges, and future directions are deliberated upon in the adoption of blockchains for sustainable supply chains. Researchers should undertake case studies across various sectors to analyze blockchain’s scalability and its effects on ethical sourcing and sustainability. The exploration of regulatory frameworks to support blockchain adoption in compliance-heavy industries is imperative.

articleTitle: Supply Chain Innovation on Acceleration Decision-Making, The Mediating Role of Tech and Integration in the Retail Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study examines the significance of supply chain dynamism in improving decision-making in the retail sector in Jordan with a special focus on technological and organizational integration as moderating variables. Supply chain dynamism is acknowledged to be one of the pivotal factors in successfully navigate through the complex world of retail today, however, its effect on directly improving decision making has not been looked into. This paper examines the level of dynamism within supply chains in the Jordanian retail industry, presents key determinants for enabling effective SC decision-making, and highlights the interaction between those dimensions, along with collaboration which mediated through Technology & Organizational integration. Results show that greater supply chain dynamism leads to better decision-making with complementary nature of technology and organizational process integration. The research provided recommendations for practitioners to improve decision-making and performance in the case of the Jordanian retail sector through supply chain dynamism and technological and organizational integration.

articleTitle: Heavy-Tailed Distributions: Their Impact on Noncontiguous Allocation and Job Scheduling in 2D Mesh NoCs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Multicore system on chip has led to the evolution of many research areas due to the advances in circuit technology design and performance issues. Mesh topology is the most common template that was proposed for the communication of the network on chip due to its scalability and simplest form. This paper investigates the effect of bounded pareto job size distribution on the performance of well-known non-contiguous allocation strategies (GABL, Random, MBS, Paging (0)) based on different communication patterns (Near Neighbor, One to All, and Random) and various scheduling strategies (First-Come-First-Served (FCFS), Out-of-Order (OO), and Window-Based) in 2D mesh NoCs. The results show that the performance of the non-contiguous allocation strategies is improved when the distribution of job size is bounded pareto. Also, the results for the two job size distributions considered (i.e. uniform distribution and bounded pareto distribution) show that GABL, MBS, and paging (0) allocation strategies outperform Random allocation strategy. Moreover, the results reveal that the scheduling strategies OO and window-based improve the system performance over FCFS scheduling and also near neighbor communication has the best performance among other communication patterns considered in this research work.

articleTitle: Legal Aspects, Public Interest, and Legitimate Interest in Processing Personal Data to Operate Autonomous Car
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The UAE 2021 Data Protection Law (DPL) and the European Union’s GDPR are not just regulatory frameworks but groundbreaking attempts to regulate personal data management. They extend their scope to emerging technologies like autonomous vehicles, once a figment of science fiction but now a global reality. Just as the GDPR demands explanations for data controller algorithms under Article 22, the DPL must revolutionize its regulatory approach to address privacy concerns related to autonomous vehicles. This paper embarks on a journey through the legal intricacies of processing personal data in autonomous vehicle operations, specifically focusing on the distinction between processing data for public interests and legitimate interests. The analysis dives deep into the definitions of personal data and special categories of personal data as outlined in DPL Chapters 1 and 5 and Article 3, which exempts personal data processing related to state security, public safety, and national defense. By examining these provisions, the paper aims to shed light on how data protection laws apply differently depending on the purpose of data processing. This comprehensive analysis enriches understanding of current data protection frameworks. It provides insights for future legislative developments or modifications to the DPL, ensuring robust personal data protection in the era of advanced technologies.

articleTitle: Offline signature verification using lightweight deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The biometric approach to signature verification serves as the foundational method predominantly employed for personal purposes in validating significant documents and legal transactions within both private and governmental sectors. Detecting counterfeit signatures is of paramount importance; however, manual methodologies reliant on subject matter experts entail substantial time, effort, and expense, making them susceptible to errors and requiring significant expertise. Addressing these challenges, this thesis presents advancements in offline signature detection and verification, considering devices with limited resources and inadequate samples of collected signatures.The proposed model utilizes lightweight deep-learning techniques to classify signatures as genuine or forged, achieving a delicate balance between high accuracy and resource constraints. In this study, four lightweight deep learning models were employed: MobileNet V3, MobileNet V2, Mobile Net V1, and EfficientNetB0. These models were evaluated on two datasets: GPDS, the largest signature database in the field, and FHD, which was specifically compiled for research purposes as a challenge and incentive. Results indicated that MobileNet V3 outperformed its predecessors and EfficientNetB0 in terms of accuracy and practicality, achieving an accuracy rate of 87.48% on the GPDS dataset and 86.75% on the FHD dataset.The relevance of this research lies in providing an effective and reliable tool to aid decision-making in the field of biometrics and signature verification, crucial across all sectors requiring individual authentication and verification. This contributes significantly to overall management and the attainment of satisfactory quality standards.

articleTitle: Exploring Healthcare Students’ Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) in the healthcare sector presents significant opportunities and challenges. As AI technologies evolve, it is essential to understand the perspectives of future healthcare practitioners who will be at the forefront of this transformation. This study explores the perspectives of medical science students and future healthcare practitioners regarding AI. Questionnaire was used to collect the data and descriptive statistical analysis was used to answer the research questions. The analysis of participants responses confirms that future healthcare students generally hold positive attitudes toward AI integration in healthcare and highlights an educational gap, with most participants lacking formal training on AI in healthcare. These results underscore a critical need for targeted AI education in healthcare curricula to foster acceptance, address concerns, and prepare students effectively for AI-integrated careers.

articleTitle: Filling the Gaps: A Comprehensive Review of Image Inpainting
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Image inpainting refers to the technique of restoring missing or damaged regions of an image while maintaining its overall visual coherence. This involves reconstructing lost or corrupted areas using a range of methodologies. In this paper, we introduce an overview of the public techniques ranging from traditional to modern techniques. The current paper offers an overall review of the state-of-the-art in image painting, evaluating the strengths and limitations of various approaches. Our goal is to introduce a piece of valuable information about image restoration, to encourage researchers to work in this field.

articleTitle: IoT Security Based On Lightewight Cryptographic (LWC) Algorithms: A survey
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The Internet of Things is millions of devices that communicate with each other and transmit sensitive information between them. The information is collected through the sensors on these devices, and is transmitted between the devices via the Internet. However, ensuring security in terms of authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, authentication, and data integrity is considered one of the challenges facing the Internet of Things, because ensuring these matters is through encryption, and traditional encryption algorithms are not suitable and cannot be applied in the Internet of Things environment, which is characterized by limited resources, so it was necessary From searching for algorithms suitable for the limited Internet of Things environment. In this paper, a comparison will be made between the literature studies conducted in this field in terms of challenges and possible solutions, in an attempt to find the gaps in them.

articleTitle: Digital Evidence and Forensic Tools in Cyber Law: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The exponential rise in hacking, phishing, information theft, and electronic crime has become an actual concern with the increased use of digital devices and technology. By 2023 the number of IoT devices expectation will be 32.1 billion devices, leading to a significant increase in cybercrimes. These illegal behaviors are specifically connected to computers and communication technology. Consequently, there has been an urgent need for the development of cyber law which is a legal system closely related to digital evidence. This paper aim to provides delve into the significance and multifaceted applications of digital evidence within the context of cyber law, shedding light on the complexities and nuances inherent in its acceptance and reliability. The paper explores the importance and numerous uses of digital evidence in the context of cyber law, highlighting the challenges associated with its legitimacy and acceptance. Additionally, it focuses on the challenges that prevent digital evidence from being seamlessly incorporated into court processes and offers solutions and strategic advice to overcome these challenges.

articleTitle: Dynamic Exit Selection and Counting Area Adjustment for Efficient Crowd Evacuation in Asymmetrical Layouts
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative methodology to address the significant challenge of evacuating large crowds from buildings with multiple exits, particularly in scenarios with asymmetrical exit configurations and high population densities. The proposed model incorporates dynamic counting areas that adjust according to evacuee density, alongside a probabilistic exit selection mechanism influenced by enhanced dynamic parameters—congestion, distance, and empty. It also accounts for heterogeneous agent behaviors to more accurately represent evacuee dynamics in complex, asymmetrical environments with dense crowds. Key findings indicate that the model effectively alleviates bottlenecks at congested exits, optimizes exit usage, and enhances overall evacuation safety. Comparative analyses demonstrate that the proposed model significantly improves evacuation efficiency and reduces travel distances compared to previous models. Simulation results indicate that agent density directly affects evacuation time, with lower congestion levels facilitating faster egress. These advancements lead to more precise evacuation time predictions and crowd flow assessments, offering valuable insights for refining emergency egress strategies in complex settings. Future research will focus on refining the model with real-world data to expand its applicability in diverse settings, such as stadiums and public transportation hubs, thereby enhancing emergency preparedness and response.

articleTitle: Explainable AI for Epileptic Seizure Prediction: A SHAPE and LIME Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological chaos typified by frequent, spontaneous seizures. Early recognition of epilepsy by utilising AI techniques to scan EEG signals can enhance the prevention and management of it. This study aims to improve the classification of epileptic seizures by using the preprocessed version of the Epileptic Seizure (ERS) dataset. The preprocessed dataset is subjected to multiple stages in order to improve its quality and achieve balanced class representation. Data cleaning, outlier management, merging, and oversampling are those. After that, an 80:20 split of the dataset is made into subsets for testing and training. Next, training, testing, and evaluation are performed on the models of Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC), Decision Tree Classifier (DTC), Random Forest Classifier (RFC), CatBoost Classifier (CBC), and ExtraTree Classifier (ETC). The ExtraTree Classifier is remarkably accurate, with a 99.51% accuracy rate, which is the highest accuracy. Finally, explainable artificial intelligence (SHAP and LIME) is used to clarify the ExtraTree Classifier's decision-making procedure. By providing a visual representation of significant variables and their influence on the model's predictions, this interpretability tool improves comprehension of the classification results.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning in Mental Diseases Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Mental diseases, mental disorders, or psychological disorders is a large group of symptoms which causes changes to the state of mood and reflect this on the behavior of the person with the mental disorder. It affects the patient’s way of thinking, which limits his ability to perform his simple daily needs, and thus, becomes a burden on the individual, and on the surrounding society as well. There are common types of mental disorders such as depression, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder. In this research, two main objectives are considered. The first objective is determining which is the best classifier for predicting a person’s mental disorder among six well-known classifiers. The second objective is determining what is the best feature selection technique to use with mental disorders datasets considering six popular techniques, and with respect to several evaluation metrics. The results revealed that Logistic Regression and Naïve Bayes are the two best classification models, while Info Gain Ratio is the best feature selection method.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Network Infrastructure for a Multi-Branch Organization Using Cisco Packet Tracer
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Designing and simulating a network infrastructure for multi-branch organizations is essential for ensuring seamless connectivity and efficient operations. This paper addresses the challenges faced by organizations in maintaining consistent and reliable network connectivity across multiple locations, including managing network traffic, ensuring security, and optimizing resource allocation while keeping costs under control. The study presents a comprehensive methodology involving the conceptualization of network ideas, designing the network architecture, adding necessary devices and tools, configuring these devices according to the network topology, and troubleshooting to ensure optimal performance. Key elements such as VLANs, routers, switches, and routing protocols like RIP, OSPF, and EIGRP are incorporated, with the entire design and simulation conducted using Cisco Packet Tracer. The findings demonstrate that full connectivity between headquarters and branch sites can be achieved within a budget of $40,000. This paper provides a practical guide for implementing similar network projects, emphasizing the importance of detailed configurations and troubleshooting steps, and recommends adopting this methodology to enhance network infrastructure efficiently and cost-effectively.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering and Model-Based Systems Engineering Frameworks for Managing Requirements of Systems of Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Goal-oriented requirements engineering (GORE) for Systems of Systems (SoS) includes combining individual operational systems local goals to achieve higher-level goals. GORE offers a structured approach to managing complex requirements, ensuring that strategic goals are translated into operational tasks. This paper provides a review of GORE frameworks, including those incorporating Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), that could be used in the management of complex Systems of Systems. The paper analyzes recent GORE frameworks such as CGS4Adaptation which combines Goals and SysML for managing adaptive Socio-Cyber-Physical Systems (SCPSs); GORE-based approach to Energy Management Systems (EnMS); Model-Based and Goal-Oriented Approach for the conceptual design of smart grid services; GORE and reference architecture approach for microgrid systems; and Adaptation-Oriented Requirement Modeling approach (ADORE). A comparative analysis is conducted to assess the extent of effectiveness these frameworks provide for improving SoS traceability, adaptability, and system design integrity. The paper concludes with key findings on the strengths and limitations of the considered frameworks, on the basis of which, major conclusions on how GORE combined with MBSE can be used for managing SoS requirements in Smart Grid (SG) and socio-cyber-physical systems could be drawn. This review paper also contributes to the requirements engineering domain by outlining effective strategies for designing and managing complex, adaptive Systems of Systems.

articleTitle: State of the Art on Auto Electrification
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper presents a full analysis of the state of electrification technologies today, including a synopsis of recent developments and new trends. Electrification is essential to the transformation of many industries, as well as transportation, manufacturing, and residential uses given that the world is moving more and more toward sustainable energy. This paper compiles data from a variety of sources, including academic journals, business analyses, and technology advancements, to provide a comprehensive overview of the most recent advancements in electrification. This review includes the delineating essential tenets of electrification and its importance in accomplishing objectives related to energy efficiency and environmental sustainability. The changing picture of electrified transportation is then examined, including electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, and creative mobility alternatives.

articleTitle: Application of Big Data Analytics in Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan: Perspectives on the Mobile Telecommunications Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This study purposes to investigate the usage of big data analytics in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan from the perspective of the mobile telecommunications industry. Additionally, it improves the acquisition of knowledge over big data. This research is carried out by formulating research questions and then extracting research objectives according to them to be used in this research. Besides, this research was created using a survey design. The population of this research consisted of a total of 3,396 staff polled from telecommunication firms in Jordan, that are Umniah, Orange, and Zain. The instrument used for data collection was a questionnaire, where data from completed questionnaires was subjected to percentage analysis. The findings of the research demonstrate that revenue generation via data analytics is changing in the Jordanian telecom industry as a result of big data. The report recommends that firms in the telecoms industry would benefit by providing their staff with data analysis tools and encouraging them to come up with new ways to look at it.

articleTitle: Harnessing ML and NLP for Enhanced Cybersecurity: A Comprehensive Approach for Phishing Email Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Emails stand as a predominant mode of online communication, facilitating the exchange of information. With the ubiquity of emails, there has been a marked rise in unsolicited messages, particularly phishing emails. These deceptive emails aim to mislead recipients, often masquerading as trustworthy entities, to extract confidential information. Embedded with dubious offers, advertisements, malicious links, malware, and trojans, perpetrators deploy these emails with malicious intent, primarily to commit fraud. Consequently, distinguishing between phishing attempts and genuine emails becomes paramount. This study constructs machine learning-based models to detect phishing emails, ensuring accurate discernment between genuine and fraudulent messages. Leveraging two datasets, the Fraud Email Dataset and the Phishing Email Dataset, we developed and evaluated classifiers, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and SVM. The Random Forest model emerged as the most effective, achieving accuracies of 98.72% on the Fraud Email Dataset and 99.15% on the Phishing Email Dataset, demonstrating strong generalizability across diverse phishing patterns. These results underscore the efficacy of ensemble methods for enhancing cybersecurity by reliably detecting phishing emails.

articleTitle: Enhancing Skin Cancer Detection Across Skin Tones with Style Transfer Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Skin cancer, accounts for a significant number of cancer-related deaths, with early detection being critical for improved outcomes. However, existing artificial intelligence (AI) models for skin lesion detection often underperform for individuals with darker skin tones due to biases in dermatology datasets. To address this, we developed a method that incorporates U-Net-based segmentation to isolate skin lesions and arbitrary style transfer to augment the dataset with diverse skin tones. Using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), our system classifies seven different skin diseases from the HAM10000 dataset. Our approach achieved an accuracy of 0.89, improving detection performance across varied skin tones and lesion types.

articleTitle: Multi-class classification algorithm for ocular diseases classification based GLCM texture features
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Ocular diseases cover a broad spectrum of conditions impacting eye health and functions, potentially resulting in vision impairment or blindness. Common eye diseases include cataracts, glaucoma, and Diabetic Retinopathy. The World Health Organization estimates that there are around 94 million people globally with significant visual impairment or blindness due to cataracts; approximately 7.7 million people have glaucoma, and 3.9 million people have Diabetic Retinopathy. This work uses machine learning (ML) techniques to detect ocular disorders, including Diabetic Retinopathy, cataracts, and glaucoma. Gray-Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM) feature optimization in the images allows for feature extraction and classification. The suggested method is evaluated using 2776 categorized photos gathered from diverse sources. These extracted features are then classified using ML models, including k-nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Neural Network (NN), Gradient Boosting (GB), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF). The classification accuracies of the ML models in training phase were DT 99%, GB 86%, k-NN 57%, ANN 60%, and RF 99%.

articleTitle: Advancing Stroke Prediction: Explainable Machine Learning Models and Data Augmentation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Stroke, a leading global disability cause, affects 12 million people annually, with 6.5 million dying. Preventing at least half of strokes requires public policy action and increased awareness. Early diagnosis is crucial and enhances patients' opportunities to survive a stroke. This research looks into how well machine learning (ML) models can predict when strokes will happen and how data augmentation affects those predictions.. Five ML models (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBoost, and Random Forest) are assessed and their performance is compared using an imbalanced and augmented dataset. Data augmentation techniques, including Random Oversampling, SMOTE, and Cluster Centroids, are employed to address class imbalance. The results demonstrate that some models achieve relatively high accuracy without data augmentation (XGBoost: 0.95). However, data augmentation techniques further improve performance across all models. Random Oversampling leads to the highest Accuracy for Random Forest (0.99), while SMOTE achieves the best Precision for Logistic Regression (1.00). The results found that age, occupation type, BMI, blood glucose level, and history of cardiovascular disease are risk factors for stroke. This study highlights the effectiveness of ML models, particularly when combined with data augmentation, for stroke prediction and emphasizes the importance of specific features in identifying stroke risk.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Insulin Management: A Digital Health Solutions for Type 1 Diabetes Support
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Type 1 diabetes is characterised by a deficiency of pancreatic beta cells, resulting in hyperglycemia and insulin deficiency. It usually develops during childhood or adolescence, but symptoms can appear much later. The specific origin of type 1 diabetes is still unknown, but T cell-mediated beta cell death is thought to be responsible for the monogenesis of the disease. New treatments such as insulin pumps, continuous glucose monitoring and hybrid closed-loop systems are being developed. Tight glycemic control has reduced the incidence of microvascular and macrovascular disorders. However, most T1DM patients continue to experience these problems and significant research efforts are needed to improve the quality of life and prognosis of T1DM patients through early diagnosis, prevention of beta cell depletion and better treatment options. Exogenous insulin therapy is needed in this disease to avoid the devastating consequences of hyperglycemia. Psychological issues and comorbidity management are elements of good T1D care, proper nutrition, diabetes treatment, and comprehensive diabetes education. Additionally, several challenges must be overcome at different stages of life. Managing T1D with limited resources Healthcare professionals deal with various difficulties at work. Nonetheless, an alphabetical approach can achieve the best outcome and enable comprehensive T1D care in a scenario where resources are scarce. In the management of children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), effective glycemic control is crucial since it is associated with improved short- and long-term health outcomes. However, poor glycemic control lowers quality of life and increases the risk of acute and chronic issues.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wireless Communication with Compact SIW Resonator-based UWB Fork Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The rapid expansion of wireless communication across networks and devices, driven by advancements in the Internet of Things (IoT), highlights the need for compact, lightweight, cost-effective, and efficient antennas to meet market demands and support wireless systems. Patch and substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) antennas have emerged to address these needs. In this study, a substrate-integrated waveguide resonator is used to construct an ultra-wideband (UWB) fork monopole antenna. The SIW resonator enhances antenna performance and bandwidth while reducing weight and dimensions. A prototype antenna was designed, manufactured, and evaluated through experimental tests. The impact of integrating array holes into the antenna on bandwidth characteristics is also examined. Significant performance improvements are demonstrated by the proposed SIW-based UWB fork monopole antenna. Simulations and experimental results show a bandwidth improvement of up to 10.1 GHz, an S11 value reduction to -47.5 dB with one array of holes, and a gain increase to 4.9642 dB. These metrics confirm the antenna's effectiveness in overcoming traditional bandwidth limitations and improving overall performance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Three Different Operators for Object Highlighting in Medical RGB Images: Canny, Roberts, and LoG in Independent Color Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The research presents a comparative analysis of the selection of objects of interest in color medical cytology images. For these purposes, the individual edge detection operators studied are Canny, Roberts, and LoG. The comparison contrasts the standard method of assessing color photographs with a technique that incorporates supplementary information. Data from individual color channels, derived from the breakdown of a color image in RGB format, serve as supplementary information. The following individual cases for potential examination are emphasized: Image processing with a complete level of reuse of edge detection operators; with a partial level of reuse of edge detection operators. The results are displayed through an array of tables, graphs, and images. Metrics of visual perception of images are utilized for comparative analysis. Compared with traditional edge detection methods, the proposed approach yields better results, which can exceed the estimates of the classical approach by 20%.

articleTitle: Building Trust: The Role of Strategic Decision-Making in Digital Market Confidence
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This research aims to explore the impact of digital marketing on enhancing confidence among consumers in the Jordanian markets, focusing on the mediating role of strategic decision-making. As the business landscape is progressively becoming digital, businesses use a variety of online advertising tools to build trust between their target audience and also build relationships and positive perceptions of their brand. This research follows a mixed-method approach using quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews with consumers and marketing professionals in various industries within Jordan. The results show that good digital marketing practices, e.g. personal communication, interesting content and customer service based on responsiveness have a great impact on consumer confidence. Also, the research defines strategic decision-making as an essential mediator that moderates the connection between direct marketing activities and buyer confidence. These results bookend a broader picture where adopting strategic frameworks for decision-making by businesses leads to better alignment of digital marketing strategies with consumer needs and preferences which in turn, contributes to increased confidence levels prevalent in the market. Several implications that are of significant value to marketers and businesses in Jordan: as shown by this research, the importance of embedding strategic decision-making in digital marketing strategy; these measures can contribute to increasing customer confidence which leads to rewarding market outcomes.

articleTitle: Machine Learning as the Shield: Mitigating ARP Poisoning Attacks in Software Defined Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) revolutionizes network management by centralizing control, but this centralization also introduces notable vulnerabilities, especially Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) poisoning attacks. These attacks exploit the ARP protocol, redirecting network traffic to malicious destinations. This research provides a deep dive into the nuances of these threats within the SDN context, outlining their mechanisms and potential countermeasures. A significant highlight of this paper is exploring Machine Learning (ML) as a pivotal mitigation approach. By analyzing and distinguishing between benign and malicious traffic patterns in real-time, ML models present a robust solution to enhance SDN security. The findings of our paper underscore the criticality of integrating these advanced predictive techniques in SDNs, paving the way for a safer and more resilient networking future.

articleTitle: A MOEA/D Framework Based on Memory Differential Cooperation Mechanism for Dynamic Multiobjective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: In this paper, a new framework based on memory differential cooperation mechanism is proposed. It effectively combines the memory mechanism, differential evolution algorithm and cooperation mechanism, and makes improvements according to the characteristics of MOEA/D to promote MOEA/D make full use of the historical evolution direction and PS distribution. Firstly, this paper designs a memory mechanism method to record the past historical information effectively, and selects the excellent individuals in the historical information as the guide group. Secondly, the differential cooperation mechanism will guide the population to decompose each subpopulation, and use the differential algorithm to iteratively optimize the subpopulation to search the Pareto set suitable for the current environment. Thirdly, through the idea of cooperation algorithm, the excellent individuals of each subpopulation are further shared to replace the individuals of this population, which further improves the convergence and diversity of the algorithm. Finally, extensive testing is conducted on FDA, dMOP, and F test suites. Experimental results show that exceeds the performance of some state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Parallel Approach for Cloud Service Broker Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Cloud Services Brokers (CSBs) manage and organize access to the resources offered by Cloud Service Providers (CSP). As the number of cloud services and users is growing dramatically, operation costs increase proportionally, and that might incur a degradation in the Quality of Service (QoS), which leads to Service Level Agreement (SLA) violations. In this paper, a parallel hybrid metaheuristic approach based on Hill Climbing (HC) and the Greedy Approach is proposed. The approach aims to create energy-efficient schedules that allow CSBs to manage access to cloud resources. The approach was evaluated in terms of parallel runtime, speedup, and energy efficiency. The approach achieved 26x speedup using the same 256 KB dataset on 256 processors. It was also proved that the proposed algorithm is energy efficient.

articleTitle: Using Artificial Intelligence Techniques in Law Enforcement: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with law enforcement has improved humane safety and crime prevention. It offers numerous applications, including predictive policing, facial recognition systems, natural language processing, and algorithmic decision-making tools, which can improve crime prevention and resolution. However, the employment of AI creates ethical problems concerning privacy, bias, and accountability. Addressing these challenges is vital to guarantee AI applications conform with legal and ethical standards, encouraging public trust. This survey paper reviews some of the tools and techniques of AI used in law enforcement (Criminal Identification, Virtual Crime Scene Reconstruction, Automated License Plate Recognition (ALPR), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Gunshot Detection Systems, Data-driven Policing Strategies), and explains the challenges, and mentions some opinions regarding this use.

articleTitle: Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) in Arabic using Lexical-Semantic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Semantic text similarity has a crucial role in natural language understanding (NLU), which is intended to evaluate the semantic and relatedness of two texts and produce a similarity score. Frequently, the Arabic short text consists of very few words, which mean that they usually do not provide adequate data in understanding the sentences. There are many difficulties and challenges that face processing and understanding of the Arabic short texts. The representations of Arabic short text of different lengths are investigated using lexical-semantic technique to eliminate the less informative words. In this paper, a hybrid approach that combines word-based features and text-based features is proposed for MSA Arabic short texts. It is based on lexical and semantic analysis. Semantic relatedness uses the Feature Vector (FV) Model, which is generated by acquiring semantic features of the word and the context. A comprehensive evaluation is done and the accuracy of the links between concepts is enhanced. The results shows that the lexical and Semantic knowledge is important in understanding short text.

articleTitle: Escape Rooms and E-Learning Unite for Smart Cities Education Entertainment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Smart cities adopt innovative educational methods to give citizens the required skills and knowledge. This paper explores integrating e-learning and Artificial Intelligence Technology related to escape rooms as an educational methodology developed to improve education in smart cities. Integrating the interactive and educational problem-solving elements of escape rooms with the flexibility of e-learning that adopts a mixed-method approach aims to enhance participation, critical thinking, and collaborative learning. This study demonstrates the main factors affecting these combined technologies integrations and the existing studies used for this purpose. The study examines the effectiveness of this hybrid educational model through a comprehensive review of the literature, followed by a discussion of its potential applications and benefits in the context of smart cities. The results indicate that this combined approach can significantly enhance cutting-edge learning outcomes to better prepare individuals for the complexities of living and working in smart cities.

articleTitle: Unveiling Deception: Different Strategies for Combatting Arabic Fake News
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: the proliferation of fake news has become a widespread problem in the contemporary era of information, posing possible harm to public discussions, political stability, and community confidence. To tackle this difficulty, it is necessary to develop strong and effective detection methods that can accurately recognize misinformation in several languages, including Arabic. The aim of this study is to create and assess different models specifically designed for the identification of fake news in Arabic language.Several of deep Learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long short-term memory (LSTM), Bidirectional long short term memory (Bi-LSTM) and convolutional neural network (CNN) are used in this study. On the other hand, some of the traditional machine learning models like k-nearest neighbors (KNN), Random Forests (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), decision tree (DT) and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) are also used. Also, transformers, like Generative pre-trained Transformer 3 (Gpt-3) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), are used as a feature extraction to convert text into numerical representation and assign different number to each token. All of these models were used in evaluation which of them is the best model in the process of fake news detection for the Arabic Language Dataset.The findings demonstrate strong performance across deep learning models, with CNN-LSTM, Bi-LSTM and CNN-Bi-LSTM exhibiting the best accuracy rates of 93.2% ,92.6%, 93.6% respectively. The LSTM model achieves a moderate accuracy of 87.4%, whilst the RNN model demonstrates a more modest accuracy of 56.8%. The results emphasize the capability of deep learning methods in reducing the dissemination of fake information in Arabic-language datasets.

articleTitle: Securing Internet of Vehicles IoV Communications: A Biometric and Hash-Key Derivation Function HKDF-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: In light of advancements in the Internet of Things (IoT), the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has emerged as a crucial component in developing autonomous vehicles. However, the rapid evolution of this technology has introduced significant security concerns. This paper addresses the growing threat of cyberattacks on autonomous vehicles that utilize wireless communication networks. The proposed model introduces a novel solution to safeguard driver privacy and secure network connections during vehicle operation by employing the driver’s biometric information and Hash-Key Derivation Function (HKDF) (HMAC-based Key Derivation Function) to generate a unique session key. This approach fills a critical research gap by enhancing the security of automated vehicle communication systems vulnerable to various cyber threats. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in creating a robust and unpredictable network key, significantly increasing the difficulty for attackers in compromising the system.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of VANET Attacks: Predictive Models, Vulnerability Management, and Defense Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET) is a critical network in the Internet of Things (IoT) era, as it plays a key role in enhancing road safety by broadcasting alerts between vehicles to prevent accidents and save lives. However, due to VANET's open structure, limited infrastructure, and various security vulnerabilities, messages can be intercepted, forged, or disrupted by malicious attacks. This paper proposes an "operation room" framework designed to enhance VANET security by addressing these threats. First, we identify the most common attacks, including Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS), Denial of Service (DoS), spamming, Black Hole, Gray Hole, Sybil, Man-in-the-Middle, ID Disclosure, and the dissemination of bogus information, which exploit VANET's vulnerabilities. In the second stage, we propose integrating the operation room with the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), Roadside Units (RSUs), and On-Board Units (OBUs) to enhance attack detection and mitigation capabilities. This operation room is equipped to identify and neutralize these threats. Finally, we discuss the challenges of detecting and responding to such diverse attacks and outline measures for protecting driver privacy and network integrity.

articleTitle: A secure IoT limited Devices by applying Multi-Round Lightweight Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is considered the base factor, that helps in developing many sectors. Additionally, IoT provides novel applications and services, i.e. smart homes, connected cars, and industrial automation. However, this development aggravates the security and privacy issues. This is because the connected devices may be vulnerable to cyber attacks in addition to generated data. Accordingly, it is of utmost importance to deploy appropriate security measures to alleviate these attacks. To overcome the mentioned problem, this work employs lightweight cryptography on limited processing capabilities of IoT devices i.e. limited memory, computing power, and battery life. These limited capabilities obstruct employing cryptography methods that require nontrivial computational resources. This work presents a multiround lightweight cryptography approach for IoT devices, which defines the security and protection of generated and transferred data. Multi-round cryptography mitigates the required device resources while ensuring robust protection and maintaining the stability of IoT devices.

articleTitle: Detection of Thyroid Disease Through Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Thyroid disease, one of the most common endocrine disorders, requires prompt diagnosis to effectively treat it. To improve diagnostic precision and expedite medical procedures, this paper explores the use of Machine Learning (ML) approaches for the early identification and categorization of thyroid diseasees. Sophisticated machine learning methods, including support vector machines, neural networks, and decision trees, are used to leverage a variety of datasets. These models outperform traditional diagnostic techniques in their capacity to identify complex patterns and minute variations in thyroid function parameters. The application of machine learning to the diagnosis of thyroid disease not only increases diagnostic accuracy but also makes preventive healthcare approaches possible. Personalized risk assessments are made possible by ML models, which analyze a wide range of patient-specific characteristics and help to improve the targeting of therapies. Furthermore, decision-making procedures are accelerated by the real-time processing powers of machine learning systems, which may shorten the interval between diagnosis and the start of therapy. this paper emphasizes how machine learning has revolutionized the diagnosis of thyroid disease and how it has the potential to completely change clinical procedures. The integration of sophisticated algorithms and extensive datasets presents opportunities for enhanced precision, effectiveness, and customization of diagnostic methods, which might eventually lead to better patient outcomes and more efficient use of healthcare resources for thyroid condition treatment. In this paper, the results were as follows: Two classifiers performed the best: LMT and LogitBoost. The Trees and Meta-learning strategy performed the best learning strategy, while the CorrelationAttributeEval and InfoGainAttributeEval methods performed the best feature selection.

articleTitle: Classification of Sleep-Related Disorders Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Several people suffer from irregular sleep patterns, a problem that negatively affects their daily lives. It presents a multitude of challenges, including daytime distress, disturbances in sleep-wake patterns, feelings of unease, and a variety of other complications. Diabetes, obesity, and psychological disorders are among the diseases that may be responsible for this sleep disorder. Therefore, the primary aim of this research is to employ the robust capabilities of machine learning in forecasting sleep disorders. This research classifies three diseases: diabetes, obesity, and psychological disorders, using thirty-two different classifiers belonging to five learning strategies. The research compares and evaluates their predictive performance on four datasets. The comparative analysis includes four evaluation metrics: Accuracy, Precision, ROC Area, and MCC. The research results indicate that the best classifier is SGD, followed by LMT, while NBM is the weakest classifier. In addition, the research results revealed that the best strategy is Functions, followed by Rules, with Bayes being the least effective strategy. While conducting the experiment and analyzing the data, it is observed that the best feature selection method that yielded the most favorable outcome is the CorrelationAttributeEval. Furthermore, it has been found that the classification algorithm known as SGD achieved the highest Accuracy and Precision in categorizing the data. This indicates that the combination of CorrelationAttributeEval as the feature selection approach and SGD as the classification algorithm proved to be the most successful and efficient strategy for this research

articleTitle: Usage of Blockchain Technology for Improving Computer Security
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Cyber threats have grown increasingly sophisticated, surpassing the capabilities of traditional security measures. Blockchain technology, with its decentralized and immutable structure, offers a potential solution to these challenges. This study examines the role of blockchain tools such as smart contracts, decentralized identity management, and secure data sharing in enhancing cybersecurity. A review of key literature and analysis of survey data from cybersecurity professionals demonstrate blockchain's effectiveness in improving data integrity, access control, and secure communications. The results show significant correlations between the adoption of blockchain technologies and the mitigation of threats like data breaches and unauthorized access. While blockchain presents promising advancements, scalability, regulatory barriers, and energy consumption remain challenges. The study provides valuable insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers on how blockchain can be integrated into modern cybersecurity strategies to create more secure digital environments.

articleTitle: Guidelines to Develop a Cybersecurity Policy in Schools, Perspectives Informed from Jordanian Cybercrime Law
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: For educational institutions the introduction of the Jordanian Cybercrime Law No. 17 of 2023 added an extra dimension of stricter legal compliance to the already challenging task of developing cybersecurity policies. As a response, this paper presents guidelines to support the education sector in this regard. What underpins this work is the knowledge gained from a comprehensive examination of the current state of cybersecurity practices in Jordanian schools. Then, combining case studies, insight from expert consultations, and a review of Jordanian cybercrime legislation informed the guidelines on how schools should approach effective cybersecurity policy and implementation. The findings combine essential elements which span strategy, standards, hardware and software, and training. A core theme of these guidelines is how legal compliance can be achieved for school policies in relation to Jordanian Cybercrime Law and the negative effects of non-compliance. These outcomes have ramifications for school administrators and policymakers to acknowledge the urgent need to integrate legal and educational strategies to strengthen their cybersecurity practices. The intent of this recommended framework is for Jordanian schools to strike a balance complying with national cybercrime laws and fostering a secure educational environment. This proactive approach has a dual purpose. Institutions can be protected from cyber threats and in doing so promoting a culture of cybersecurity awareness among students and staff. However, this framework relies on administrators and policymakers to navigate the complexities of digital security in educational environments.

articleTitle: From Interaction to Action: How User Input Shapes Logistics and Decisions in Jordan’s E-Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The main purpose of this research is to investigate how logistics affect the decision-making cascade of Jordan's e-industry through user interaction. The research investigates the impact of logistics performance through different user interaction stages, from seeking information to purchasing decisions, boosting interaction and communicating with users. Methodology: This research has followed a quantitative approach based on data collected from selected e-commerce businesses in Jordan. The research explores the effect that logistical considerations, including delivery speed, shipping accuracy, and cost efficiency combined with user experience elements, have on consumers' decision processes within a digital market space. It shows that in e-commerce, the most important factor that affects your decision-making is logistics. Making matters worse is that user interaction also mediates this relationship. Effective and transparent logistics, engaged through channels to make communication and responsiveness easy. Makes it much easier for the user to transact faster. The findings of this study could also deepen the understanding of logistics in digital industries and enhance decision-making by integrating user interaction. Practical implications. The study's findings offer practical implications for Jordan's e-commerce companies and logistics providers. This trust results in repeat purchases and improved customer experience: the service is quicker, and the results are more reliable. This work's practical contribution is in helping practitioners formulate their logistics and interaction strategies.

articleTitle: Smart Contract Security Vulnerability Through The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The invention of the smart contract has advanced the transaction system due to its transparency and immutability. However, it also raised many concerns when the source code was vulnerable. Many detection and repair tools have been developed to tackle these issues, yet they must still be appropriately standardized. This paper created a security procedure, adapting one of the most trustworthy cybersecurity standards, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0. There are 38 reviewed studies through the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) protocol, which will be arranged and classified with NIST CSF 2.0 functions as the output. This paper suggested the application of NIST CSF 2.0 as a smart contracts development standard to ensure the robustness of the contract. Moreover, this paper provides future work to enhance the approaches' scalability in discovering new threat or attack patterns.

articleTitle: TKG-RAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework with Text-chunk Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The approach of dividing text into chunks and building indexes is a mainstream approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, retrieved text chunks often contain noise or redundant information, which can negatively impact RAG performance. To address this limitation, researchers have proposed RAG approaches based on text chunks, knowledge graphs, and long-texts. Nevertheless, there are still challenges that need to be addressed, such as the underutilization of knowledge within text chunks, the resource-intensive nature and complex process of constructing Knowledge Graphs (KG), and the lack of emphasis on optimization during the post-processing filtering stage. We propose a RAG framework with text-chunk knowledge graph (TKG-RAG). The proposed framework can construct a text-chunk knowledge graph automatically by extracting the hierarchical structure, contextual relationships, topic sentences, and inter-chunk relationships from the domain text. The framework begins by using text indexing to retrieve relevant text chunks based on similarity. These chunks are then mapped to nodes within the text-chunk knowledge graph, where connections are established based on the relationships of nodes in the graph to generate subgraphs. The content of the nodes is rearranged and merged using the hierarchical structure and relational knowledge in the graph, and then the residual isolated nodes that are not merged are fused based on the attribute knowledge in the TKG. In addition, to improve the performance of filters in the post-processing stage, we incorporate the datasets considering texts and numerical characteristics, into the fine-tuning process of the filter model. This approach aimed to enhance the accuracy of filtering and reduce token consumption in the generation stage. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, comparative and ablation experiments were conducted on five datasets: NQ, PopQA, HotpotQA, TriviaQA, and LawQA. The results show that TKG-RAG can achieve better performance in terms of Accuracy and F1 scores, while also reducing token consumption by 46%, means that TKG-RAG can combine the strengths of chunk-based and graph-based RAG approaches.

articleTitle: Detecting Spam and Malware Using BERT and LLMs
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Spam and malware hinder the growth of IT and its use in many facets of contemporary life. This work employs directional Encoder Representations Transformers (BERT) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance the detection of spam and malware. Researchers use cutting-edge Natural Language Processing (NLP) to detect malicious information with exceptional precision and resistance. BERT is an open-source NLP and Machine Learning (ML) framework. Text around unclear phrases help computers grasp context. It uses transformers, a Deep Learning (DL) model with dynamic weightings that connects all output and input elements. LLMs and BERT are used to identify SMS Spam and Malware using memory samples in this study. In the experiments, BERT demonstrated excellent performance on the datasets it used. By using BERT on SMS spam and malware datasets, accuracy of 100% and an F1-score of 99.99% for spam detection, alongside an accuracy of 100% and an F1-score of 100% for malware detection. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that BERT and LLMs have the potential to revolutionize cybersecurity, digital threat mitigation, and natural language processing classification.

articleTitle: Multi Label Classification Algorithm Based on Conditional Local Correlations among Labels and Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: Multi-Label Classification (MLC) is an advanced form of traditional classification, where each data instance is simultaneously associated with multiple labels. The importance of MLC has increased significantly in recent years, due to its wide range of application areas. Modern algorithms, when faced with the challenge of multiple labels, continue to show suboptimal performance, conversely, they show significantly superior performance when processing single-label datasets. This paper proposes a new algorithm to deal with the problem of transforming datasets from multiple labels to single labels by exploiting conditional and local correlations between labels after applying the Apriori predictive algorithm to extract relationships. Six ensemble learning models: Voting Hard, Voting Soft, Voting Weighted, Stacking LR, Stacking RF, and Stacking SVM, along with four classification models: SMO, DecisionStump, Random Forest, and Random Committee, were applied to three datasets. The algorithm showed effective and good performance by comparing the results of the proposed Multi Label Classification algorithm based on Conditional Local Correlations among Labels (MLC-CLCL) with several popular algorithms for dealing with multiple labels.

articleTitle: Research into the accuracy of complex sensorimotor responses of operators to joystick-run technological equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: This paper analyses the impact of visual information presentation methods on a human operator's control of remote technological objects, specifically focusing on the perception of information from electronic displays and the operator's immersion in a virtual environment, as it relates to the accuracy of joystick handle positioning. Experiments employed psychophysiological evaluations of accuracy and speed related to visual-motor tracking using joysticks. The findings revealed no discrepancies in the accuracy and speed of visual-motor tracking between groups participating in tests using information from electronic displays and those interacting with virtual environment. The paper provides recommendations on using virtual environments and displaying information on electronic screens for various operator tasks.

articleTitle: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection and Classification Using Deep-wavelet and multiple classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 25th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
abstract: The eyes, being the most intricate and indispensable sensory organs, serve as a window for gathering external images which are transformed to signals and delivered to the brain through the optic nerves. There are many diseases can affect the human eye. Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is one of these eye diseases especially affecting people with diabetes. It caused a thickening of the outer retinal layer and is known to have different levels of severity. In recent times, automatic classification of certain ophthalmologic and cardiovascular diseases using analysis of retinal images has become commonplace within telemedicine settings. In this paper we proposed a novel methodology in two stages for the classification and detection of Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) along with various severities of the disease using deep wavelet as a tool for feature extraction (FE) techniques with modalities such as KNN, SVD and for detection and classification tasks. The dataset used is the Diabetic Retinopathy Grayscale Images dataset from Kaggle .In our case, we conclude that our approach is performing reasonably and provides a good results according to the comparative estimate.
